title: RetroPaint use cases and user stories
scope: Normative intended behavior grounded in local source inspection. No application execution claims.

chapters.name: Getting started and protecting a picture
chapters.benefit: learn by trying things while keeping control of my picture
chapters.contract: Opening a control or changing a preference must not add paint. Destructive document changes must have a recoverable outcome. Basic mode is a simpler interface, not a separate document format.

chapters.name: Brushes spray smudge and erasing
chapters.benefit: express a particular mark rather than fight the painting tool
chapters.contract: A pointer gesture is one edit. Paint follows paper coordinates at every zoom. Affected regions include the tool footprint, while unrelated layers and pixels stay unchanged. Random tools need distribution and containment checks rather than identical screenshots.

chapters.name: Colours textures gradients and live ink
chapters.benefit: choose materials that make my picture feel alive and keep their meaning when I save it
chapters.contract: Material selection affects future marks unless an explicit edit is active. Freeze time when comparing rendered animation frames. Static image downloads capture one frame; projects retain the supported live definitions, with the specific rainbow baking exception described in decisions.

chapters.name: Shapes symmetry stamps and Spiro
chapters.benefit: turn playful experiments into deliberate patterns and illustrations
chapters.contract: Shape and pattern previews must remain temporary until their normal completion action. Every selectable family has a parameter expansion in the coverage matrix. Changing a pattern tool does not recolour the paper.

chapters.name: Selections text and image transformations
chapters.benefit: arrange and revise an illustration accurately without losing the source
chapters.contract: A preview is distinguishable from a committed edit. Whole picture and selection scope must be explicit. A raster placed beyond paper is trimmed deliberately; editable vector geometry has a different retention rule. Test both rather than expecting one behavior everywhere.

chapters.name: Layers and mixed picture composition
chapters.benefit: separate parts of a picture and change one part without damaging the others
chapters.contract: Layer order, identity, visibility, opacity, paper transparency and active target are part of the document. Palette visibility is workspace state. Changing one must not silently change the other.

chapters.name: Editable vector and raster pieces
chapters.benefit: keep individual parts adjustable as my illustration becomes more ambitious
chapters.contract: Raster and vector describe how new marks are created, not a command to destroy existing pieces. Object transforms must stay nonsingular. Pixel effects on one selected piece must not flatten its neighbours.

chapters.name: Photo lab workflow light and looks
chapters.benefit: improve a photograph while keeping the original available for another try
chapters.contract: Photo edits are saved recipes on the selected sheet. Done commits the draft, Cancel discards that draft, and Before is a comparison. Original pixels and hidden crop margins must remain recoverable. A photograph need not look better to every viewer: acceptance checks isolate the effect being requested.

chapters.name: Photographic colour balance and curves
chapters.benefit: make intentional colour choices and understand what changed
chapters.contract: Use known neutral patches and coloured samples as well as natural photographs. Separate channel and combined curve effects. Values outside the accepted range must never enter a saved recipe as nonfinite numbers.

chapters.name: Photo detail effects geometry and lens corrections
chapters.benefit: refine a photograph without mistaking display tricks for changes to its saved source
chapters.contract: Detail needs source resolution checks. Geometry can alter a layer within a shared document frame. Crop retains source margins in projects. Grain must be stable between renders, not a random animated overlay.

chapters.name: Files exports projects and local recovery
chapters.benefit: keep independent copies and return to work with its intended editability intact
chapters.contract: A download event is not proof of file correctness. Save the actual bytes, decode independently and reopen through the visible file workflow. Reject malformed inputs before replacing the live document. Local draft recovery is separate from an independent project file.

chapters.name: Larger enhanced image copies
chapters.benefit: judge generated detail before keeping a larger copy of my work
chapters.contract: Enhancement creates a separate image copy. It does not resize flatten or replace the editable document. The source is the finished visible composition. Generated detail is estimated and must be compared with the original.

chapters.name: 3D workshop basics transforms and layers
chapters.benefit: turn a simple idea into an accurately placed editable solid
chapters.contract: Millimetres are model units, independent of paper pixels and camera zoom. A visible mesh is not enough: appropriate cases require independent bounds, volume and closed surface checks. Workshop operations must respect the active CAD layer, locked state and busy state.

chapters.name: 3D sketches dimensions constraints and boolean building
chapters.benefit: describe a shape by its dimensions and make predictable additions and cuts
chapters.contract: Sketch dimensions drive geometry rather than act as labels. Supporting faces are geometric references, not transient triangle numbers. Joins and cuts must honour entered endpoints while preserving a valid solid. Use independent analytic checks for simple fixtures.

chapters.name: 3D history shells edge finishes lofts and sweeps
chapters.benefit: refine an earlier design and preserve its construction instead of rebuilding it from scratch
chapters.contract: Preview rebuilds a temporary complete result. Apply commits one coherent edit. Cancel leaves the saved recipe and original solid intact. Failed or timed out precision operations must not apply partial geometry. Surface checks include real cavities and edge references, not only a successful triangulation.

chapters.name: 3D inspection mixed pictures STL import and print preparation
chapters.benefit: check a model honestly and use it in both a picture and a printable file
chapters.contract: Camera changes and inspection are separate from model geometry. STL stores tessellated geometry without source sketches or colours. Checks must examine the exported file independently, including cavity orientation and dimensions. Slicer preparation and physical printing remain external steps.

chapters.name: Responsive input accessibility comfort and resilience
chapters.benefit: keep creating comfortably across devices and recover from interruptions
chapters.contract: These are normative usability and reliability requirements. Source presence is evidence of an entry point, not proof of accessibility compliance. Keyboard drawing equivalence, browser permissions and hardware behavior need explicit capability notes rather than invented support.

chapters.name: Complete creative journeys across experience levels
chapters.benefit: finish something meaningful while keeping a path back to the editable work
chapters.contract: These journeys intentionally combine smaller cases. They count as integration use cases, not as additional proof that each component has passed. Keep every intermediate saved artifact so a failure can be located at the correct transition.

PLAY.name: Ready painting paper
PLAY.preparation: Create a fresh 960 by 640 document with one opaque white Paper sheet. Use Raster mode, symmetry Off, no crop, no saved photo recipe and no live ink unless the steps ask for them. Keep a clean copy. Record size, Strength, applicator, colour and device input for each gesture. Use paper coordinates rather than screen coordinates.
PLAY.availability: Preparation specification; fixture bytes must be created or supplied and hashed before a run

PATCH.name: Known pixels and alpha
PATCH.preparation: Create a 960 by 640 RGBA PNG. Use a transparent background and labelled nonoverlapping rectangles at integer coordinates: red #FF0000 at x100 y100 width100 height80, blue #0000FF at x400 y100 width100 height80, green #00FF00 at x100 y300 width100 height80, and 50 percent alpha red at x400 y300 width100 height80. Add a one pixel black border on a separate copy where required. Keep opaque white and opaque black backing copies for edge inspection. Save the exact generator recipe, bytes and hash before testing.
PATCH.availability: Preparation specification; fixture bytes must be created or supplied and hashed before a run

PIXEL.name: Crisp pixel art
PIXEL.preparation: Create a 32 by 32 PNG with no alpha, only black white red and blue. Include a one pixel staircase from x2 y2 to x15 y15, a one pixel wide vertical line, and a four by four checkerboard. Enlarge the paper view without changing the source. Use the original 32 by 32 bytes as the oracle for source pixels, not a screenshot of an enlarged canvas.
PIXEL.availability: Preparation specification; fixture bytes must be created or supplied and hashed before a run

FILL.name: Connected regions and tolerance
FILL.preparation: Create a 320 by 240 RGBA image with a black one pixel rectangle from (20,20) through (140,140), a pale grey #E8E8E8 interior and white outside. Put a second disconnected pale grey island at (220,40) sized40 by40. Keep separate copies with a one pixel gap at (80,20), antialiased edges, a transparent island, and deterministic interior variation of plus or minus 8 channel levels. Document the flood similarity metric observed in source before choosing boundary colours for exact tolerance tests.
FILL.availability: Preparation specification; fixture bytes must be created or supplied and hashed before a run

SMUDGE.name: Two wet colour regions
SMUDGE.preparation: Use a transparent 320 by 240 sheet with an opaque red rectangle x40 to140 and opaque blue x160 to260, both y60 to180, and clear margins. Create both wet live and settled versions when supported. Trace a fixed horizontal drag from (120,120) to (200,120) at recorded size and Strength. The oracle checks local displacement, unchanged outside regions and alpha, without assuming random texture bytes are identical.
SMUDGE.availability: Preparation specification; fixture bytes must be created or supplied and hashed before a run

MIX.name: Multilayer picture
MIX.preparation: Use a 960 by 640 document with Paper, an opaque blue Backdrop, a transparent Character sheet with red and green known patches, and a transparent Caption sheet with text and a stamp. Set Character opacity to0.5 in the relevant variant. Give every layer a unique name. Add a separate copy with live water and conveyor ink plus a saved photo recipe and editable objects. Save a baseline project and a controlled time composition.
MIX.availability: Preparation specification; fixture bytes must be created or supplied and hashed before a run

VECTOR.name: Mixed editable scene
VECTOR.preparation: Start from PLAY, choose Vectors, and create separately named rectangle, concave heart, line, text, stamp, Spiro path, transparent imported PNG and two independent raster brush gestures. Place several overlaps and one item partly outside the paper. Record object IDs kinds transforms original raster dimensions and layer order from a baseline project, plus an independent rendered reference.
VECTOR.availability: Preparation specification; fixture bytes must be created or supplied and hashed before a run

PHOTO.name: Photographic editing source
PHOTO.preparation: Use a legally usable local photograph at least1600 by1200 with a horizon neutral object dark detail bright detail fine texture and some varied colour. Record provenance bytes dimensions decoder and SHA256. Keep an untouched independent copy. Pair it with the synthetic TONAL COLOUR DETAIL and GEOMETRY fixtures for objective checks. A tiny synthetic patch cannot substitute for the natural photograph when judging ringing composition skin colour or photographic appearance. No private photo is included in this documentation.
PHOTO.availability: Preparation specification; fixture bytes must be created or supplied and hashed before a run

TONAL.name: Known luminance ramp
TONAL.preparation: Create a 1024 by256 RGBA image containing an opaque 0 through255 neutral ramp with four columns per value. Add separately defined uniform patches at32 64 128 192 and224 and fully transparent padding in a second copy. For exposure, compute linear light from the published sRGB transfer equation independently, multiply by2 for plus1 EV or0.5 for minus1 EV, clamp, then reencode. Histogram bins and clipping counts come from the independently decoded result.
TONAL.availability: Preparation specification; fixture bytes must be created or supplied and hashed before a run

COLOUR.name: Hue and neutral samples
COLOUR.preparation: Create opaque patches for red orange yellow green aqua blue purple magenta and neutral levels32 128 and224. Include near boundary hues on both sides of red wrap and every mixer band. Include a grey patch deliberately cast by known channel gains and semitransparent versions with unchanged alpha. Save the exact RGB and alpha values and positions. Use a natural photo separately for appearance checks.
COLOUR.availability: Preparation specification; fixture bytes must be created or supplied and hashed before a run

DETAIL.name: Edges texture and reproducible noise
DETAIL.preparation: Create at least1024 by768 pixels with a sharp black to white edge, fine alternating lines, broad soft edges, flat neutral areas and coloured boundaries. For noise use a documented deterministic PRNG and seed12345, store both clean and noisy pixels, and measure variance in fixed interior regions away from borders. Add a transparent coloured edge copy. Do not generate a new noisy input for each comparison.
DETAIL.availability: Preparation specification; fixture bytes must be created or supplied and hashed before a run

GEOMETRY.name: Coordinate and lens chart
GEOMETRY.preparation: Create a 960 by640 numbered grid with unique corner colours, a horizon with a known slope and a centred rectangle. Retain exact landmark coordinates. Create separate known barrel pincushion perspective and red blue channel offset variants with an independent documented mapping. Use full source data, not a previously cropped screenshot, to test retained crop margins.
GEOMETRY.availability: Preparation specification; fixture bytes must be created or supplied and hashed before a run

IMPORT.name: Image format matrix
IMPORT.preparation: Prepare genuine independently encoded PNG JPEG WebP BMP GIF and uncompressed 8 bit TIFF RGB RGBA and greyscale files. Use asymmetric orientation labels and known dimensions. Include a source with an embedded orientation tag where the browser decoder supports it. Keep corrupt truncated and unsupported compressed TIFF variants separately. Record decoder limitations and never simply rename a PNG extension to create a valid format fixture.
IMPORT.availability: Preparation specification; fixture bytes must be created or supplied and hashed before a run

LEGACY.name: Provenanced old project files
LEGACY.preparation: Collect genuine saved fixtures for every project version the current importer explicitly supports, starting with version1, from repository history or archived app builds. Record the producing revision and an expected rendered reference. Include old recipes with missing later optional fields. These fixtures are a planned requirement until such bytes exist: changing the version number of a current project is not valid migration evidence.
LEGACY.availability: Preparation specification; fixture bytes must be created or supplied and hashed before a run

CORRUPT.name: Disposable invalid inputs
CORRUPT.preparation: Create copies of valid fixtures and independently alter one property at a time: truncate bytes, corrupt an image data URL, duplicate IDs, introduce NaN or invalid numeric encodings, singular object transforms, invalid crop bounds, broken workplanes, unsupported recipe kinds, mismatched STL counts and open mesh edges. Keep an unrelated unsaved picture open in a disposable session for atomicity comparison. Never damage the users original files.
CORRUPT.availability: Preparation specification; fixture bytes must be created or supplied and hashed before a run

LIMIT.name: Boundaries in a disposable session
LIMIT.preparation: Use small fixtures to establish behavior first. Test image edge4096 and4097, sheet count16 and17, and stored pixel budget64000000 at the nearest reachable valid and invalid combinations. Three4096 squared sheets use50331648 pixels and a fourth would exceed the budget. Check draft pixel and character cutoffs separately. For CAD exercise128 top level pieces, 2 and16 loft profiles, 2 and64 path points, 64 constraints and their first invalid counts. Record machine memory and stop safely on allocation failure; do not allocate giant structures just to claim coverage.
LIMIT.availability: Preparation specification; fixture bytes must be created or supplied and hashed before a run

NETWORK.name: Controlled local resource capture
NETWORK.preparation: Use a clean disposable browser profile or storage namespace on the intended app origin. Record browser version app revision network requests methods origins and request sizes. Run once uncached and once with assets cached. Keep source image and model hashes so any outgoing data can be identified. Permission denial network interruption and missing asset tests must be controlled reversibly. Do not expand host exposure or change user security settings to make a check pass.
NETWORK.availability: Preparation specification; fixture bytes must be created or supplied and hashed before a run

CAD.name: Known simple solids
CAD.preparation: Use a new 3D layer in a 960 by640 picture. A primitive20 mm cube is centred X0 Y0 Z10, with bounds[-10,-10,0] to[10,10,20] and analytic volume8000 cubic mm. Include a 20 by10 by30 asymmetric wedge or labelled rectangular solid for view and transform checks. Use no nonuniform scale or earlier features unless specified. Record units and recipe plus an independently decoded triangulated surface.
CAD.availability: Preparation specification; fixture bytes must be created or supplied and hashed before a run

JOIN.name: Exact positive and negative pull
JOIN.preparation: Use the CAD20 mm cube. Place a centred10 by10 rectangle on fixed XY at Z0, then union its extrusion with the cube. Positive pull30 produces bounds Z0 to30 and volume9000 cubic mm. Negative pull-10 produces bounds Z-10 to20 and volume9000 cubic mm. For face recesses use a10 by10 top face sketch cut5 mm, removing500 cubic mm. Preserve entered values and compare far endpoints independently.
JOIN.availability: Preparation specification; fixture bytes must be created or supplied and hashed before a run

BOOLEAN.name: Analytic overlap and cutter
BOOLEAN.preparation: Use cube A bounds[0,0,0] to[20,20,20] and cube B bounds[10,0,0] to[30,20,20]. Each volume is8000, overlap is4000, union12000, subtraction of B from A4000, intersection4000 and convex hull12000 cubic mm. Add a separate inside cylinder cutter and disjoint copies for scope tests. Keep an asymmetric target name so subtraction order is unambiguous. For an independent Hull versus Union discriminator, use two 10 mm cubes with bounds [0,0,0] to [10,10,10] and [20,0,0] to [30,10,10]. Hull volume is 3000 cubic mm and union volume is 2000 cubic mm, with a genuine 10 mm gap between source pieces.
BOOLEAN.availability: Preparation specification; fixture bytes must be created or supplied and hashed before a run

HISTORY.name: Nested editable construction
HISTORY.preparation: Build a named source body, an attached dimensioned rectangle or circle, a Through all hole, a supported small edge finish, and a separate shell version. Save a known valid baseline with unique feature IDs and at least enough separate steps to force paging. Keep variants with loft and sweep profile constraints. The baseline must already be geometrically checked before testing a downstream rebuild so source defects cannot be blamed on a later edit.
HISTORY.availability: Preparation specification; fixture bytes must be created or supplied and hashed before a run

SHELL.name: Joined cube and cylinder plus simple shell oracle
SHELL.preparation: Cube20 by20 by20 has centre[0,0,10]. Cylinder diameter20 height20 has centre[15,0,10], so the union has outside bounds[-10,-10,0] to[25,10,20] and a complex planar top cap. Shell the top inward by3 mm. Check floor height3 and wall offsets using independent section rays in straight curved and junction regions, not a single approximate total volume. Repeat with bottom cap. For the one third diameter overlap variant use cylinder centre X=40/3 mm, giving overlap depth20/3 mm at the cube right edge. Separately shell a simple20 mm open top cube: remaining volume4668 cubic mm. Retain unmodified source unions inside project recipes.
SHELL.availability: Preparation specification; fixture bytes must be created or supplied and hashed before a run

CADMIX.name: Solid picture and guide
CADMIX.preparation: Use a 960 by640 picture with Paper, a green opaque Backdrop or a local guide photo, one CAD layer containing the SHELL joined model, and a transparent Paint above3D sheet with text and a coloured arrow. Save a known camera view in both perspective and orthographic variants. Set source photo adjustments and a shared crop in separate copies. Layer order must be exactly documented before comparing front and back picture canvases.
CADMIX.availability: Preparation specification; fixture bytes must be created or supplied and hashed before a run

STL.name: Independent mesh input
STL.preparation: Prepare genuine binary and ASCII tetrahedra cubes and a simple closed curved mesh with known coordinates. Include a2 unit cube for unit scaling and an offset copy for centering. Build counts at 200000 triangles and200001 separately where feasible, and byte sizes at 20000000 and20000001. Use an independent encoder, preserve source hashes and record the manifold status. A valid large disconnected solid collection is distinct from a corrupt high count file.
STL.availability: Preparation specification; fixture bytes must be created or supplied and hashed before a run

HOLLOW.name: Nested oriented mesh shells
HOLLOW.preparation: Create an independently encoded outer cube10 mm edge, an inner fully enclosed6 mm cavity, a nested2 mm material island and a separate4 mm cube away from them. Analytic total signed material volume is1000-216+8+64=856 cubic mm. Produce variants with all faces reversed, one face reversed, mixed component winding, permuted triangles and both binary and ASCII encoding. Require manifold edges and independent containment checks. Never use the importer under test to build the expected oriented result.
HOLLOW.availability: Preparation specification; fixture bytes must be created or supplied and hashed before a run

variants.execution_rule: Exercise every entry on desktop and touch layouts. Symmetry is a modifier family as well as a main illustrated control.
Run tap slow curve fast curve size endpoints strength endpoints and Undo for each actual applicator. Test random materials with fixed seeds where available.
Each needs stationary and moving input, edge clipping and release/cancel checks.
Use both opaque Paper and a transparent sheet where the effect supports alpha. Each mode gets an independent before state.
Every shape requires forward/reverse drag, tiny and normal bounds, fill/outline combinations and Undo. Polygon polyline and spline use their explicit point completion workflow.
Every active repeat count needs an asymmetric off axis motif. Test Mask on/off and a working sector boundary.
Exercise paint and supported fill behavior. Freeze times for frame comparisons, and distinguish the two animated textures from static textures.
Enter Bucket first because the gradient tray is context sensitive. Test preset stops and user endpoints separately.

Test every individual stamp at least once in raster and editable mode where supported. Emoji glyph rendering depends on platform; assert recognizable presence and identity before pixel comparisons. Do not count one stamp per bank as all stamp coverage.

Each gear and offered hole needs a valid drawing check. Cover each stator and outer tooth choice, plus pairwise combinations and documented invalid combinations; do not claim the full Cartesian product unless run.
Test slot replacement capacity reverse zero speed and stable save/reopen. A serialized legacy rainbow-time recipe is import compatibility coverage, not proof of an exposed new UI control.
Exercise the meaningful combinations with explicit scope; reject unavailable combinations honestly.
Each font and property needs a visible result and project persistence check. Record fallback fonts rather than inventing identical glyphs across platforms.

Exercise default minimum maximum and a meaningful intermediate value for every exposed scalar using its declared source range. Crop coordinates are covered by their frame contract, not as unrelated global sliders.
Every group must be reached through the real UI in desktop portrait and short screen navigation.
Custom is an indicated state, not an extra preset action. Test each actual selectable value and saved baseline behavior.
Exercise every offered ratio on portrait and landscape sources, with edge clamps, rounding and Cancel. Original ratio depends on the actual source dimensions.
Open real fixtures and independently decode real downloads. Record lossy palette alpha and TIFF limitations per format.
Use small deterministic samples for broad combinations and separately run whole image boundary tests with recorded resource constraints.
Each primitive needs bounds volume closed surface and save/reopen, not merely a visible thumbnail.
Test each direction, positive and negative coordinates, locked pieces and transformed world bounds. Extra copies means count plus the original, not total count.
Every supported constraint needs actual rebuilt geometry, persistence and a conflict variant. Diameter applies to circle sketches, other line constraints to appropriate noncircle outlines.
Use analytic simple cases and nontrivial joined cases. Check every operation target semantics and boundary orientation.

Expand each supported feature editor and its original sketch/path child nodes. Not every kernel combination is supported; unsupported combinations must preserve the original and explain the limitation.
Separate view-only checks from physical geometry checks. Inspect every exported scope and every nested shell orientation variant independently.
Test accepted boundary and first rejected boundary in disposable sessions; exact limits are source baseline values, not forever frozen product design.
Use explicit supported browser and hardware records. Cover high risk combinations exhaustively and lower risk interactions pairwise; do not claim every Cartesian combination unless executed.

cases.title: Find the paper and make a first mark
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to find the paper and make a first mark, so I can learn by trying things while keeping control of my picture.
steps: Open a fresh session without a saved preference
Choose the illustrated Brushes tool and a bright colour
criteria: Paper is ready without an account or mandatory tutorial
The tool and chosen colour are visibly selected
A single gesture produces a mark and enables Undo
cases.exception: A returning recovery prompt must leave the ready canvas usable until the user chooses to resume.

cases.title: Choose tools by picture and name
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to choose tools by picture and name, so I can learn by trying things while keeping control of my picture.
steps: Open its choices and select one
Close the choices and return to the paper
criteria: Each tool has a meaningful label as well as its illustration
The selected tool is distinguishable without colour alone
Opening choices does not move or mark the picture
cases.exception: Choosing the already active tool may open or close its drawer but must not erase its settings or artwork.

cases.title: Keep my picture when I open More
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to keep my picture when I open More, so I can learn by trying things while keeping control of my picture.
steps: Open More and visit File Image Advanced and View
Close More and continue the mark
criteria: The same document remains active throughout
Drawers do not flatten layers or reset ink
Continuing the stroke uses the intended current tool
cases.exception: Clicking outside a drawer closes only that drawer and does not create an unintended canvas mark.

cases.title: Undo my last complete action
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to undo my last complete action, so I can learn by trying things while keeping control of my picture.
steps: Make three separate strokes in three colours
Redo the undone actions in order
criteria: Each Undo removes one complete user action
Redo restores its placement colour and appearance
The earlier strokes remain unchanged
cases.exception: After Undo followed by a new stroke the abandoned Redo branch must not reappear.

cases.title: Keep an established picture instead of clearing it
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to keep an established picture instead of clearing it, so I can learn by trying things while keeping control of my picture.
steps: Make a mark and allow artwork age to exceed 120 seconds
Choose Keep drawing and then try Escape
criteria: The confirmation names the destructive action
Keep drawing has safe initial focus
Both dismissal paths retain every layer and editing state
cases.exception: Repeated Clear presses must not stack several dialogs or accidentally accept the destructive option.

cases.title: Clear deliberately and recover with Undo
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to clear deliberately and recover with Undo, so I can learn by trying things while keeping control of my picture.
steps: Open the Clear confirmation on an established picture
criteria: Clear has one defined document outcome rather than leaving stale visible fragments
Undo restores all affected pixels live ink and editable content
Redo repeats the same clear outcome
cases.exception: Repeat on a newly started picture where the current app may clear immediately: a clear must remain undoable even when no age warning is shown.

cases.title: Grow into Advanced mode without losing work
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to grow into Advanced mode without losing work, so I can learn by trying things while keeping control of my picture.
steps: Disable it then enable it again
criteria: Layers and Photo lab become discoverable in advanced mode
The underlying layers recipes and picture do not change when controls hide
The chosen mode is remembered on this device
cases.exception: Basic hides vector authoring and the 3D workshop as well as Layers, Photo lab and enhancement. Enable Advanced to enter 3D; it then exposes Layers. Switching back to Basic preserves saved advanced content and creates new raster artwork. This mode boundary supersedes the earlier auto-promotion behavior by user request on 2026-10-29.

cases.title: Understand what is selected and editable
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to understand what is selected and editable, so I can learn by trying things while keeping control of my picture.
steps: Select a normal paint sheet then a hidden sheet
Select an editable object and finally a CAD layer
Inspect the target and available actions each time
criteria: The target is named before an edit
Hidden targets and unavailable actions have visible explanations
Paint object and solid selection are not confused with one another
cases.exception: Typing into a name field must not trigger a drawing or CAD shortcut.

cases.title: Resume after help without changing my tool
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to resume after help without changing my tool, so I can learn by trying things while keeping control of my picture.
steps: Choose a stamp and its size
Open shortcut help and browse every category
Close help with Done or Escape
criteria: Help fits the available screen
Focus returns to a meaningful control
The selected stamp size and picture survive
cases.exception: While the dialog is open ordinary drawing and document shortcuts must not act behind it.

cases.title: Keep an unavailable action understandable
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to keep an unavailable action understandable, so I can learn by trying things while keeping control of my picture.
steps: Start with no selection and one layer
Inspect selection transforms merge and Redo
Perform the setup that makes each action available
criteria: Unavailable controls are disabled or explain the missing prerequisite
Trying them leaves the document untouched
They become available when their prerequisites are satisfied
cases.exception: A stale button press during a busy operation must not create a partial edit or an extra Undo step.

cases.title: Draw a broad marker line
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to draw a broad marker line, so I can express a particular mark rather than fight the painting tool.
steps: Choose Marker at size 22 and full Strength
Draw a curve then a short tap
criteria: The curve is continuous with rounded joins
The tap leaves one intentional mark
The size preview corresponds to the affected paper area
cases.exception: Rapid pointer samples must not produce holes or join the end of this stroke to the start of the next.

cases.title: Sketch with a biro
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to sketch with a biro, so I can express a particular mark rather than fight the painting tool.
steps: Choose Biro and a dark colour
Make slow and fast curved strokes
criteria: The biro produces its own visibly finer pen character
Curves follow the hand
Switching applicators does not change previous marks
cases.exception: Returning from Spray restores a drawing applicator rather than spraying under a biro label.

cases.title: Make calligraphy with a shaped nib
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to make calligraphy with a shaped nib, so I can express a particular mark rather than fight the painting tool.
steps: Draw horizontal vertical and diagonal strokes at one size
criteria: Stroke character depends on the nib direction
Joins remain continuous
Changing colour affects only subsequent marks
cases.exception: Sharp turns and very short strokes must not create huge spikes or an unpainted gap.

cases.title: Paint with textured poster colour
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to paint with textured poster colour, so I can express a particular mark rather than fight the painting tool.
steps: Choose Poster Paint and fill a small area with strokes
criteria: The mark has visible material texture rather than a flat marker clone
Overlap responds consistently to Strength
Undo restores the first pass
cases.exception: Texture should stay attached to the picture when zoom changes rather than sliding across existing paint.

cases.title: Build a watercolour wash
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to build a watercolour wash, so I can express a particular mark rather than fight the painting tool.
steps: Make one wash then several overlaps
Wait and compare the result with a saved frame
criteria: Overlapping washes visibly build colour
Edges remain soft within the footprint
The intended wet or static appearance is retained on export
cases.exception: A nearly transparent wash must not silently become opaque when the tool is changed or the project is saved.

cases.title: Draw exact pixel art with Pencil
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to draw exact pixel art with Pencil, so I can express a particular mark rather than fight the painting tool.
steps: Draw a staircase on the enlarged pixel grid
criteria: The pencil selects its intended one pixel width
Occupied source pixels align with the grid
Reopened dimensions and exact pixel colours match
cases.exception: At fit zoom a tap still changes the intended source pixel rather than a whole screen pixel block.

cases.title: Use every classic brush character
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to use every classic brush character, so I can express a particular mark rather than fight the painting tool.
steps: Repeat the same path with Classic Brush Oil Brush Crayon and Natural Pencil
criteria: Each named tool has a distinct usable appearance
The selected sample matches the actual mark family
Old marks do not change when another classic brush is selected
cases.exception: Run each listed brush with both a tap and a bent stroke rather than treating one brush as coverage for all four.

cases.title: Control size without rescaling old artwork
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to control size without rescaling old artwork, so I can express a particular mark rather than fight the painting tool.
steps: Move the pointer at two zoom levels
criteria: The affected source footprint increases with size
The cursor indicates that footprint at each zoom
Old marks and document dimensions remain unchanged
cases.exception: Test both ends of the size range and rapid changes while the pointer is not drawing.

cases.title: Control Strength predictably
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to control Strength predictably, so I can express a particular mark rather than fight the painting tool.
steps: Draw on white and coloured areas at Strength 1 then 0.15
criteria: Lower Strength produces a weaker contribution
Overlap accumulates predictably for the selected applicator
Undo restores exact previous pixels
cases.exception: The strength label and actual active value must agree after switching tools and reopening a drawer.

cases.title: Spray fine mist
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to spray fine mist, so I can express a particular mark rather than fight the painting tool.
steps: Hold briefly then sweep across a contained area
criteria: Pigment is distributed inside the intended spray region
Holding deposits paint without requiring movement
Size changes the area rather than the paper resolution
cases.exception: A long stationary press must stop depositing immediately when the pointer is released or cancelled.

cases.title: Make splatters intentionally
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to make splatters intentionally, so I can express a particular mark rather than fight the painting tool.
steps: Choose Splatter and a bright colour
Spray near the middle then near an edge
criteria: Drops have the chosen colour and splatter character
Edge marks clip at the document boundary
One Undo removes the entire spray gesture
cases.exception: Random drops outside the paper must not wrap around to the opposite edge.

cases.title: Celebrate with coloured confetti
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to celebrate with coloured confetti, so I can express a particular mark rather than fight the painting tool.
steps: Switch to a solid colour and spray again
criteria: Rainbow bursts contain several colours
Solid bursts use the chosen solid material
Confetti remains confined to the intended footprint
cases.exception: Undo and Redo must restore the committed burst rather than generate a visibly different random arrangement.

cases.title: Smudge wet colours together
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to smudge wet colours together, so I can express a particular mark rather than fight the painting tool.
steps: Choose Smudge and drag red towards blue
Reduce Strength and repeat on a fresh copy
criteria: Paint is displaced locally in the drag direction
The edge is feathered
Weaker Strength produces a smaller displacement
cases.exception: Dragging through transparent pixels must not inject opaque black or sample another layer accidentally.

cases.title: Erase on Paper and on a clear sheet
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to erase on Paper and on a clear sheet, so I can express a particular mark rather than fight the painting tool.
steps: Repeat on a transparent paint layer
criteria: Paper erases to its defined paper colour
The transparent layer erases to alpha zero
Underlying visible layers show through the cleared region
cases.exception: Erasing a hidden sheet must not unexpectedly erase a visible neighbouring layer.

cases.title: Pull paint into a black hole
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to pull paint into a black hole, so I can express a particular mark rather than fight the painting tool.
steps: Hold and move through a painted region
criteria: The effect has a visible local shrinking or clearing action
Its scope follows the tool footprint
Release stops the effect and Undo restores the source
cases.exception: Pointer cancellation or leaving the browser must not leave the destructive effect running.

cases.title: Pixelate only the brushed area
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to pixelate only the brushed area, so I can express a particular mark rather than fight the painting tool.
criteria: Pixels inside the footprint become visibly blockier
Areas outside remain unchanged
Undo restores the original detail
cases.exception: A smaller size must not pixelate the entire image or the entire selected layer.

cases.title: Invert only the brushed area
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to invert only the brushed area, so I can express a particular mark rather than fight the painting tool.
steps: Brush once over known RGB patches
Repeat over the same region and Undo
criteria: Affected RGB values invert within the painted mask
Alpha is preserved
Two full inversions of fully covered pixels return their original RGB values
cases.exception: Partly covered antialiased edges require mask weighted comparison rather than expecting exact full inversion.

cases.title: Emboss a local texture
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to emboss a local texture, so I can express a particular mark rather than fight the painting tool.
steps: Brush across a high contrast edge
Compare the brushed and untouched areas
criteria: The effect makes a local relief appearance
Untouched detail and transparency remain intact
Undo restores the source
cases.exception: A transparent border must remain clear rather than acquiring an opaque embossed fringe.

cases.title: Finish a stroke safely outside the paper
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to finish a stroke safely outside the paper, so I can express a particular mark rather than fight the painting tool.
criteria: The first mark is clipped to the paper
Release ends the gesture even outside
The next mark starts independently
cases.exception: Repeat pointercancel lost capture and window blur with no stuck drawing state or false connecting line.

cases.title: Keep a fast pen curve smooth
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to keep a fast pen curve smooth, so I can express a particular mark rather than fight the painting tool.
steps: Draw a fast looping path with mouse and pen
Repeat while the display is busy
criteria: Available intermediate pointer samples contribute to the path
The result remains continuous
Pressure or hardware variations do not change document scale
cases.exception: An unsupported coalesced sample API must fall back to ordinary pointer input without crashing.

cases.title: Choose bright palette colours
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to choose bright palette colours, so I can choose materials that make my picture feel alive and keep their meaning when I save it.
steps: Make a short mark after each
criteria: The chosen swatch is marked selected
Marks use their chosen colours
Changing the palette does not recolour old ordinary marks
cases.exception: Run every swatch including white against a nonwhite background so an invisible mark cannot masquerade as success.

cases.title: Borrow a colour from the visible picture
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to borrow a colour from the visible picture, so I can choose materials that make my picture feel alive and keep their meaning when I save it.
steps: Sample a known composite overlap and a plain patch
criteria: The borrowed colour represents the visible composition
The magnified preview identifies the sampling area
The new swatch matches the sampled RGB value
cases.exception: Hidden layers must not influence the sampled colour and sampling must not paint a dot.

cases.title: Keep a second colour ready
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to keep a second colour ready, so I can choose materials that make my picture feel alive and keep their meaning when I save it.
steps: Set primary red and secondary blue
Right drag with a drawing tool
Right sample a green patch then swap colours
criteria: Right button drawing uses the secondary colour
Right sampling changes the secondary colour
Swap exchanges the two choices visibly
cases.exception: A browser context menu must not consume the app gesture when right button drawing is supported.

cases.title: Choose an exact hex colour
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to choose an exact hex colour, so I can choose materials that make my picture feel alive and keep their meaning when I save it.
steps: Paint and read the saved patch
criteria: The wheel swatch and numeric fields agree
The resulting fully opaque flat patch is RGB 18 58 188
The chosen colour persists after the dialog closes
cases.exception: Malformed or incomplete input must be rejected or left editable without committing a different unexplained colour.

cases.title: Choose colour with the wheel and RGB fields
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to choose colour with the wheel and RGB fields, so I can choose materials that make my picture feel alive and keep their meaning when I save it.
criteria: The marker and all displayed values agree with the chosen colour
Reopening restores the selection
Keyboard entry can reach the same result as pointer input
cases.exception: RGB bounds 0 and 255 work and values outside the accepted range cannot corrupt the active colour.

cases.title: Paint a travelling rainbow
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to paint a travelling rainbow, so I can choose materials that make my picture feel alive and keep their meaning when I save it.
steps: Draw a long curve and two separate short strokes
criteria: Several hues follow the path rather than a single solid colour
The ordering is consistent with the stroke direction
The exported frame matches the visible stroke
cases.exception: Joining samples must not produce colour discontinuities or start every segment again at the same hue.

cases.title: Choose the colour of neon
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to choose the colour of neon, so I can choose materials that make my picture feel alive and keep their meaning when I save it.
steps: Choose pink then Neon for another line
criteria: Each neon line has a bright centre and a halo of the selected tint
The blue line remains blue when pink is selected
The halo is visible in PNG
cases.exception: Partly transparent halo pixels must not become a hard opaque rectangle on export.

cases.title: Sprinkle stationary glitter
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to sprinkle stationary glitter, so I can choose materials that make my picture feel alive and keep their meaning when I save it.
criteria: Glitter has metallic looking variation
Its committed pigment does not randomly move or flash
The exported patch retains the tint and alpha
cases.exception: Comparison must distinguish stationary glitter from animated water or static texture.

cases.title: Paint every repeating texture
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to paint every repeating texture, so I can choose materials that make my picture feel alive and keep their meaning when I save it.
steps: Choose brick dots weave grass stone water and static in turn
Make a separate labelled patch for each
criteria: Each material has its named recognisable structure
Patterns tile without gross seams
Previous patches retain their material
cases.exception: Animate only materials designed to move and verify all seven textures rather than one representative texture.

cases.title: Fill a bounded connected region
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to fill a bounded connected region, so I can choose materials that make my picture feel alive and keep their meaning when I save it.
steps: Choose Bucket and a solid colour
Tap inside a closed black outline
Inspect inside outside and the line
criteria: The connected interior fills
The enclosing line and outside region remain intact
One Undo removes the fill
cases.exception: A one pixel opening intentionally allows flood propagation and must be tested separately from a truly closed outline.

cases.title: Adjust fill tolerance thoughtfully
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to adjust fill tolerance thoughtfully, so I can choose materials that make my picture feel alive and keep their meaning when I save it.
steps: Use a noisy nearly uniform interior
Fill with low then higher tolerance on independent copies
criteria: Higher tolerance includes more sufficiently similar connected pixels
Disconnected matching islands stay unchanged
The control value is visible
cases.exception: At tolerance boundaries the fill must finish without freezing or overwriting unrelated layers.

cases.title: Place a preset gradient
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to place a preset gradient, so I can choose materials that make my picture feel alive and keep their meaning when I save it.
steps: Choose Sunset Ocean Candy and Rainbow gradients in separate regions
criteria: The preset stop colours and ordering are recognisable
Colour transitions are smooth
The fill remains confined to its mask
cases.exception: Each preset must be exercised and a tiny region must not cause an invalid gradient or throw an error.

cases.title: Drag my own gradient direction
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to drag my own gradient direction, so I can choose materials that make my picture feel alive and keep their meaning when I save it.
steps: Enable Drag a gradient and choose red and blue ends
Move each endpoint pin and finish
criteria: The start and end colours correspond to their pins
Moving pins changes direction and transition within the same mask
Finishing settles one intentional result
cases.exception: A zero length drag must use a defined fallback without leaving a broken pending fill.

cases.title: Keep a pending gradient reversible
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to keep a pending gradient reversible, so I can choose materials that make my picture feel alive and keep their meaning when I save it.
steps: Create a bounded pending gradient and move both endpoint pins
Press Escape before the gradient is committed
Repeat and use the ordinary settlement or next drawing action to commit, then Undo
criteria: Escape cancels the pending gradient and restores the unchanged underlying region
A deliberately settled gradient is committed once within its existing mask
Undo restores the exact region from before that committed gradient
cases.exception: Changing tools alone may leave a pending gradient until the next settlement action in the current source. The intended contract requires that no hidden pending preview leak into a saved project. Record this transition separately and report any mismatch instead of redefining cancellation after the result.

cases.title: Build a colour conveyor
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to build a colour conveyor, so I can choose materials that make my picture feel alive and keep their meaning when I save it.
steps: Add red yellow and blue stops
Choose Snap then Ooze and paint in each mode
criteria: Snap changes between the chosen stops
Ooze blends between them
Marks use the configured sequence and direction
cases.exception: Removing stops down to an empty or one colour list must leave a usable defined material and no runtime error.

cases.title: Control the speed of living ink
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to control the speed of living ink, so I can choose materials that make my picture feel alive and keep their meaning when I save it.
steps: Change belt speed and compare fixed time intervals
criteria: The configured speed has a visible consistent effect
Ordinary solid strokes do not start animating
The picture continues rendering while live content changes
cases.exception: Speed extremes and rapid mode switches must not accumulate timers or accelerate unrelated old material unexpectedly.

cases.title: Arm live ink deliberately
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to arm live ink deliberately, so I can choose materials that make my picture feel alive and keep their meaning when I save it.
steps: Enable Live ink and make another
Disable it and make a third
criteria: Only strokes intended to use a live material carry that behavior
The armed state is visibly identifiable
The ordinary marks remain stable
cases.exception: Turning off the live control must not erase existing animation or silently bake every layer.

cases.title: Save a still from a moving picture
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to save a still from a moving picture, so I can choose materials that make my picture feel alive and keep their meaning when I save it.
steps: Prepare live water and conveyor marks
Capture one known time and download PNG
Open the PNG in a separate viewer
criteria: The file contains one coherent frame
All visible layers share the same capture time
Opening the downloaded file does not require the app to animate
cases.exception: The file must be decoded for comparison rather than accepting the presence of a download event as proof.

cases.title: Edit all eight conveyor slots and reverse its travel
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to edit all eight conveyor slots and reverse its travel, so I can choose materials that make my picture feel alive and keep their meaning when I save it.
steps: Fill the eight visible slots with chosen colours
Replace a middle slot and try adding a ninth
Set speed to negative zero and positive values
criteria: Each slot retains its intended position in the sequence
The supported eight slot capacity is enforced
Negative speed reverses travel and zero produces a stable phase
cases.exception: Clearing all slots must leave an understandable safe material fallback rather than undefined colours or a permanently armed broken ink.

cases.title: Draw straight lines and constrained lines
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to draw straight lines and constrained lines, so I can turn playful experiments into deliberate patterns and illustrations.
steps: Choose Line and drag a sloping segment
criteria: Endpoints follow the drag
Shift snaps direction to the intended 45 degree increments
One Undo removes one whole line
cases.exception: A zero length line has a safe defined tap outcome rather than invalid coordinates.

cases.title: Draw rectangles circles and ovals
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to draw rectangles circles and ovals, so I can turn playful experiments into deliberate patterns and illustrations.
steps: Drag each basic shape in both directions
criteria: Each shape fits the intended drag bounds
Shift preserves the relevant equal proportions
Reverse drags do not create negative or missing geometry
cases.exception: Exercise thin wide and tiny bounds as well as an ordinary shape.

cases.title: Choose outline and fill independently
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to choose outline and fill independently, so I can turn playful experiments into deliberate patterns and illustrations.
steps: Draw a rectangle with brush solid and no outline
Repeat with no primary and secondary fill
Compare a known inside and outside pixel
criteria: Each outline mode has the intended stroke character
Fill uses the chosen source colour
No fill preserves the background inside
cases.exception: No outline plus no fill must not secretly replace the area with an opaque default colour.

cases.title: Tell a story with geometric shapes
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to tell a story with geometric shapes, so I can turn playful experiments into deliberate patterns and illustrations.
steps: Use triangles right triangles diamonds pentagons and hexagons
criteria: Every chosen outline has the expected vertex structure
Placement is independent of earlier shapes
Redo restores the same shape
cases.exception: Small or reversed bounding boxes must preserve the selected family rather than falling back to rectangles.

cases.title: Decorate with stars hearts and lightning
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to decorate with stars hearts and lightning, so I can turn playful experiments into deliberate patterns and illustrations.
steps: Draw four five and six point stars then a heart and lightning
criteria: Each decoration is recognisably different
Concave regions are filled consistently
Downloaded appearance matches the composed image
cases.exception: Check sharp corners and internal notches for incorrect bridging or holes.

cases.title: Point with arrows and rounded rectangles
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to point with arrows and rounded rectangles, so I can turn playful experiments into deliberate patterns and illustrations.
steps: Draw arrows in all four directions and a rounded rectangle
criteria: The arrow points in the selected direction
Rounded corners remain rounded
Shape size changes do not move surrounding content
cases.exception: A very narrow arrow or rounded rectangle must remain bounded and must not invert its outline.

cases.title: Give a character a speech bubble
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to give a character a speech bubble, so I can turn playful experiments into deliberate patterns and illustrations.
steps: Choose rectangular oval and thought bubbles
Add text in the intended area
criteria: The three bubble families have appropriate outlines
The tail stays connected
Fill and text do not erase the character behind them
cases.exception: Changing the bubble family while a preview is active must not leave a stray earlier preview on the picture.

cases.title: Build a polyline and finish it
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to build a polyline and finish it, so I can turn playful experiments into deliberate patterns and illustrations.
steps: Tap four separate points with Polyline
Finish with its button or Enter
Undo then repeat with Escape before completion
criteria: Segments connect the chosen points in order
Completion produces one edit
Escape discards an unfinished path
cases.exception: With fewer than two usable points Finish must not create corrupt or unbounded geometry.

cases.title: Draw a smooth spline
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to draw a smooth spline, so I can turn playful experiments into deliberate patterns and illustrations.
steps: Choose Spline and tap a curved sequence of points
Compare with the same points as a polyline
criteria: The spline is visibly smooth rather than angular
It follows the intended control sequence
Undo removes the whole finished spline
cases.exception: Repeated or extremely close points must not cause large loops or invalid numbers.

cases.title: Close a custom polygon
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to close a custom polygon, so I can turn playful experiments into deliberate patterns and illustrations.
steps: Choose Polygon and enter an irregular outline
Complete it by the available finish action
Inspect the last to first edge
criteria: The polygon closes once
Fill remains inside the closed outline
The committed shape can be undone
cases.exception: A self crossing or degenerate outline needs a consistent safe result or clear rejection without document corruption.

cases.title: Mirror a picture across an axis
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to mirror a picture across an axis, so I can turn playful experiments into deliberate patterns and illustrations.
steps: Enable vertical symmetry and draw off centre
Repeat with horizontal symmetry on a fresh copy
criteria: Each gesture has its correct reflected counterpart
The axis passes through paper centre
Turning symmetry off affects future marks only
cases.exception: A mark on the axis must not gain an unintended darker duplicate simply because two copies overlap.

cases.title: Make every radial symmetry pattern
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to make every radial symmetry pattern, so I can turn playful experiments into deliberate patterns and illustrations.
steps: Draw one asymmetric motif in each
criteria: Each mode produces its specified number of arranged copies
Sector angles fill a full turn
One Undo removes the complete symmetric gesture
cases.exception: Use an asymmetric motif away from the centre so an incorrect repeat count cannot be hidden by coincident copies.

cases.title: Work inside a symmetry mask
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to work inside a symmetry mask, so I can turn playful experiments into deliberate patterns and illustrations.
steps: Enable Mask in a radial mode and choose a wedge
Cross its boundary then change the active wedge
criteria: The active wedge is clearly indicated
Edits respect the selected working region and corresponding pattern
Crossing a boundary does not teleport a slip into another wedge
cases.exception: Turning symmetry off must restore ordinary full paper interaction without losing earlier masked art.

cases.title: Choose a stamp from every category
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to choose a stamp from every category, so I can turn playful experiments into deliberate patterns and illustrations.
steps: Choose one visible item from each
criteria: Category navigation is usable and labelled
The selected stamp preview matches the placed artwork
No unrelated category is silently selected
cases.exception: Use the full stamp inventory expansion later to catch missing glyphs and incorrect category entries.

cases.title: Resize rotate and flip a stamp
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to resize rotate and flip a stamp, so I can turn playful experiments into deliberate patterns and illustrations.
steps: Place a stamp at two sizes
criteria: Size changes the stamp rather than paper scale
Horizontal and vertical flip directions match their controls
Fixed rotation is stable and automatic placement chooses a small random turn within the current plus or minus 14 degree range
cases.exception: Undo and Redo retain the actual committed orientation rather than rerolling automatic rotation.

cases.title: Preview a stamp before placing it
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to preview a stamp before placing it, so I can turn playful experiments into deliberate patterns and illustrations.
steps: Move the pointer around without pressing
Tap once then leave the paper
criteria: A translucent preview follows the pointer
The preview updates with settings
One tap makes one committed stamp
cases.exception: Cursor preview pixels must be absent from downloaded images and saved projects.

cases.title: Explore Spiro without changing my colours
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to explore Spiro without changing my colours, so I can turn playful experiments into deliberate patterns and illustrations.
steps: Choose a paper colour and brush ink
Open Spiro then close it without drawing
criteria: Opening the kit does not recolour existing pixels
Primary and secondary choices remain understandable
There is no new mark until an actual drawing gesture
cases.exception: An empty gear choice or cancelled drag must not deposit an accidental dot.

cases.title: Fit and move a Spiro ring
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to fit and move a Spiro ring, so I can turn playful experiments into deliberate patterns and illustrations.
steps: Move the ring away from centre
criteria: The ring follows its centre and radius controls
The numeric radius and handle agree
The paper artwork does not move with the kit
cases.exception: At the accepted minimum and maximum radius the controls remain reachable or offer a way to return the kit to view.

cases.title: Choose gears and drawing holes
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to choose gears and drawing holes, so I can turn playful experiments into deliberate patterns and illustrations.
steps: Tap a gear then select a hole
Try dragging a different gear onto the ring
criteria: The selected gear and hole are visible
The resulting path changes with the gear ratio and hole offset
Tap and supported drag selection reach the same gear
cases.exception: Dropping a gear outside its valid placement zone must not attach an unintended gear or leave a floating drag ghost.

cases.title: Wind a Spiro drawing and stop it
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to wind a Spiro drawing and stop it, so I can turn playful experiments into deliberate patterns and illustrations.
steps: Choose Auto and Wind the key
Stop or reset the kit and Undo
criteria: The motor draws the configured curve
The controls communicate whether it is running
Stopping ends drawing and Undo restores the preceding picture
cases.exception: Opening another workflow or cancelling the pointer must not leave a hidden motor changing the picture.

cases.title: Use every Spiro ring shape
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to use every Spiro ring shape, so I can turn playful experiments into deliberate patterns and illustrations.
steps: Choose Ring Oval Square and Cross
Make a short controlled pattern in each
criteria: Each stator follows its selected shape
Tooth choices affect the path predictably
Settings are reflected in controls
cases.exception: Invalid or incompatible tooth values must be constrained or explained before a broken path is committed.

cases.title: Keep a Spiro pattern editable
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to keep a Spiro pattern editable, so I can turn playful experiments into deliberate patterns and illustrations.
steps: Switch to Vectors and make a Spiro pattern
criteria: The pattern remains an individually selectable piece
Transforms do not flatten neighbouring artwork
The reopened pattern retains its geometry and material
cases.exception: Switching back to Raster must not silently merge existing editable patterns.

cases.title: Select a rectangular piece
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to select a rectangular piece, so I can arrange and revise an illustration accurately without losing the source.
steps: Move it to an empty area and Place
criteria: The selection bounds match the chosen area
The moved patch arrives at the intended coordinates
One Undo restores the pre move picture
cases.exception: A drag outside the paper clips safely and a zero area selection must not delete the image.

cases.title: Cut around an irregular subject
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to cut around an irregular subject, so I can arrange and revise an illustration accurately without losing the source.
criteria: Only pixels within the closed lasso are included
The outside background stays behind
The selection edge follows the lasso
cases.exception: Ending near the start or outside the paper must close the lasso consistently without an enormous stray region.

cases.title: Select connected colour with the wand
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to select connected colour with the wand, so I can arrange and revise an illustration accurately without losing the source.
steps: Choose Colour wand and low tolerance
Increase tolerance on a fresh copy
criteria: Selection contains connected qualifying pixels
Another disconnected matching island is excluded
The tolerance setting changes the intended boundary
cases.exception: Transparent areas and antialiased edges require explicit checks rather than treating every near colour as selected.

cases.title: Select all and invert a selection
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to select all and invert a selection, so I can arrange and revise an illustration accurately without losing the source.
steps: Select all then make a smaller rectangle
Delete the inverted region and Undo
criteria: Select all covers the intended editing scope
Invert selects the complement in that scope
Undo restores all removed pixels
cases.exception: Invert with no existing selection needs a defined full scope outcome or an explanatory disabled control.

cases.title: Copy and cut without confusing them
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to copy and cut without confusing them, so I can arrange and revise an illustration accurately without losing the source.
steps: Copy a patch and paste it
Repeat using Cut on another patch
criteria: Copy retains the source
Cut removes only its selected source
Paste creates a movable new instance
cases.exception: If the system clipboard is denied the in session copy must still be usable with an honest message.

cases.title: Place a floating raster selection
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to place a floating raster selection, so I can arrange and revise an illustration accurately without losing the source.
steps: Move a cut patch then resize its corner
criteria: Place commits the shown transform once
The floating handles disappear
Undo and Redo restore the correct source and placement
cases.exception: Changing tools uses the documented settlement rule and must not leave two copies of the same cut content.

cases.title: Cancel a floating raster selection
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to cancel a floating raster selection, so I can arrange and revise an illustration accurately without losing the source.
steps: Cut and move a piece without placing it
Compare with the saved before state
criteria: The unplaced operation is cancelled according to the raster selection contract
The original region is restored
No changed pixels survive the cancel
cases.exception: Do not apply the editable object Escape rule to an ordinary floating raster selection.

cases.title: Move and resize with clear constraints
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to move and resize with clear constraints, so I can arrange and revise an illustration accurately without losing the source.
criteria: Unconstrained resizing changes width and height independently
Shift preserves aspect ratio
Handles match the effective transformed bounds
cases.exception: Dragging through a crossed or tiny bound must not create singular transforms or lose the piece.

cases.title: Use exact selection dimensions
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to use exact selection dimensions, so I can arrange and revise an illustration accurately without losing the source.
steps: Open Image and Transform the selection
criteria: The selection reaches the entered size
Other document pixels retain their coordinates
Paper dimensions do not change
cases.exception: Blank zero negative or nonnumeric dimensions must be rejected before the edit is committed.

cases.title: Keep white transparent when placing a piece
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to keep white transparent when placing a piece, so I can arrange and revise an illustration accurately without losing the source.
steps: Copy an image with white surround and coloured centre
criteria: White background pixels follow the transparent selection policy
The coloured subject remains
Blue shows through the removed white
cases.exception: Near white and antialiased boundaries need a documented threshold or exact white rule rather than assuming automatic subject detection.

cases.title: Bring a partly lost piece back to paper
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to bring a partly lost piece back to paper, so I can arrange and revise an illustration accurately without losing the source.
steps: Drag a selected patch partly beyond each edge
Move it fully back before placement
Use Bring selection to paper when offered
criteria: The complete uncommitted source can be recovered before placement
The desk overhang is visible and draggable
The bring action centres or returns the piece without resampling it
cases.exception: Dragging from the off paper preview must reach the same selected piece rather than drawing on the desk.

cases.title: Trim a placed raster overhang deliberately
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to trim a placed raster overhang deliberately, so I can arrange and revise an illustration accurately without losing the source.
steps: Move and rotate a raster across the left edge
Move the resulting piece back and Undo
criteria: Only in paper raster content survives permanent placement
Its transform and retained source resolution are preserved
Undo restores discarded pixels
cases.exception: Repeat at all four edges and completely outside the paper with a defined empty result that does not corrupt the layer.

cases.title: Keep vector overhang recoverable
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to keep vector overhang recoverable, so I can arrange and revise an illustration accurately without losing the source.
steps: Move a vector fully beyond the paper
Place then select it through the piece list

Its piece remains addressable
Returning it restores the whole shape
cases.exception: Raster trimming rules must not be applied to vector paths or text geometry.

Neighbouring pixels stay unchanged
Undo restores exact earlier placement

All intended layers transform consistently
Export dimensions match the resulting document

Undo recovers clipped content
cases.exception: A paper size change must not secretly invoke image scaling or alter a vector's geometry.

cases.title: Choose smooth or crisp resizing

Smooth uses interpolated edges
The selected option affects the actual output

All intended document layers align to the new origin
Undo restores original dimensions and content
cases.exception: A missing selection must not crop to an arbitrary default area.

cases.title: Rotate flip and skew a whole image

criteria: Every intended layer follows the same document transform
Output bounds include the transformed content according to the operation
Undo restores layer alignment
cases.exception: Use asymmetric corner labels to expose swapped axes incorrect sign or accidental mirroring.

cases.title: Invert or remove a flat background

On another choose background removal from the top left connected region
criteria: Invert affects the intended RGB channels and preserves alpha
Background removal follows connected corner colour and tolerance
Unconnected matching islands remain

Placement follows the selected paper position
The placed caption can be transformed and undone

Set size alignment bold italic underline and strike through
criteria: Every control changes the intended text property
Alignment and line breaks are coherent
The placed image matches the preview
cases.exception: If a platform substitutes an unavailable font the outcome must remain readable and the limitation must be recorded in the test evidence.

cases.title: Give text a readable background and width

steps: Set a narrow text box and centre alignment
criteria: The width and wrapping follow the box settings
The opaque background uses the secondary colour
Transparent text leaves surrounding artwork visible
cases.exception: A very long word or empty text must not overflow controls or create an unexplained opaque rectangle.

cases.title: Use keyboard text placement without shortcuts firing
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to use keyboard text placement without shortcuts firing, so I can arrange and revise an illustration accurately without losing the source.
steps: Type letters that are also tool shortcuts
Press Ctrl or Cmd Enter to place
criteria: Typing stays in the text field
The modifier Enter action matches Place text
One Undo removes the caption placement
cases.exception: Normal Enter within a multiline text field must not unexpectedly finish an unrelated path or trigger CAD controls.

cases.title: Add and choose a clear paint sheet
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to add and choose a clear paint sheet, so I can separate parts of a picture and change one part without damaging the others.
steps: Enable Advanced mode and open Layers
criteria: A new transparent sheet appears adjacent to the working layer
Painting here identifies the current sheet
New paint affects only that sheet
cases.exception: The normal compact palette may close after an ordinary add or pick while the workshop return exception keeps it open.

cases.title: Rename a sheet meaningfully
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to rename a sheet meaningfully, so I can separate parts of a picture and change one part without damaging the others.
steps: Rename the active sheet to Character
criteria: The name appears consistently in the row target and controls
The layer ID and artwork stay unchanged
Undo can restore the previous name
cases.exception: Blank names receive a safe defined fallback and long names do not make layer controls inaccessible.

cases.title: Hide a reference without deleting it
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to hide a reference without deleting it, so I can separate parts of a picture and change one part without damaging the others.
criteria: The backdrop disappears from composition and export while hidden
Its source pixels stay intact
The foreground edit stays on its own sheet
cases.exception: Undo must restore visibility independently from later painting and the hidden layer must not contribute to colour sampling.

cases.title: Control layer opacity
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to control layer opacity, so I can separate parts of a picture and change one part without damaging the others.
steps: Choose a known red sheet above blue
criteria: The composite follows alpha blending at the chosen value
The percentage label agrees
The slider gesture forms one useful Undo action
cases.exception: Zero opacity and returning to full opacity must retain the underlying pixels and live definitions.

cases.title: Reorder by dragging the layer grip
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to reorder by dragging the layer grip, so I can separate parts of a picture and change one part without damaging the others.
steps: Move a foreground layer below the backdrop by its grip
criteria: Top to bottom display corresponds to compositing order
The selected layer identity survives
Each real reorder is reversible
cases.exception: A drop in the original position must not add a meaningless history step or duplicate a row.

cases.title: Reorder and choose layers with the keyboard
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to reorder and choose layers with the keyboard, so I can separate parts of a picture and change one part without damaging the others.
steps: Use arrows to select neighbouring sheets
Use Alt with Up or Down to reorder
criteria: Selection and order follow their separate commands
Focus remains on a meaningful row
The composition matches the resulting order
