cases.exception: Top and bottom boundaries must not wrap a reorder into the opposite end of the stack.

cases.title: Duplicate a complete layer
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to duplicate a complete layer, so I can separate parts of a picture and change one part without damaging the others.
steps: Duplicate a sheet with pixels objects live ink and a saved photo recipe
criteria: The copy starts with equivalent visible content
The two sheets have separate identities
Changes to the copy do not mutate the source
cases.exception: CAD layer duplication must also assign unique body IDs while retaining source recipes.

cases.title: Remove a sheet and undo it
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to remove a sheet and undo it, so I can separate parts of a picture and change one part without damaging the others.
steps: Select and remove a middle layer
criteria: Only the requested sheet is removed
An available remaining layer becomes active
Undo restores content order settings and identity coherently
cases.exception: Removing the last remaining layer is prevented or leaves a valid ready document rather than an empty broken editor.

cases.title: Combine two paint sheets deliberately
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to combine two paint sheets deliberately, so I can separate parts of a picture and change one part without damaging the others.
steps: Choose a paint layer above another paint layer
criteria: The displayed composition is retained at the captured frame
The resulting sheet has the defined combined scope
Undo restores separate originals and live content
cases.exception: Merging a CAD layer or merging into a CAD neighbour is unavailable so editable solids are not silently flattened.

cases.title: Export clear artwork by hiding Paper
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to export clear artwork by hiding Paper, so I can separate parts of a picture and change one part without damaging the others.
steps: Hide Paper while retaining a transparent foreground
criteria: PNG retains genuine alpha where no visible layer paints
JPEG is flattened onto white
The editable source stack stays unchanged
cases.exception: A checkerboard background used by the UI must never appear as painted squares in the file.

cases.title: Keep live layer thumbnails current
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to keep live layer thumbnails current, so I can separate parts of a picture and change one part without damaging the others.
steps: Draw one brief stroke and stop
Add live ink and observe again
criteria: The brief committed mark appears in the correct thumbnail
Animated content refreshes appropriately
Idle static pictures do not require constant full repaints
cases.exception: A hidden or offscreen palette must not stall the main painting controls or lose the next thumbnail update.

cases.title: Respect the layer and pixel limits
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to respect the layer and pixel limits, so I can separate parts of a picture and change one part without damaging the others.
steps: Add layers until the supported count or 64 million stored pixel budget is reached
criteria: The app explains the actual limiting condition
The rejected add leaves all original layers intact
Space released by removal can be used again
cases.exception: Exercise exactly 16 sheets and the nearest safe boundaries of the total pixel budget without rounding past the limit.

cases.title: Keep Layers beside the 3D workshop
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to keep Layers beside the 3D workshop, so I can separate parts of a picture and change one part without damaging the others.
steps: Open the workshop from basic mode
Toggle the backdrop eye in Layers
Use several CAD tools then close the workshop
criteria: Layers is open and interactive while paint controls behind the workshop are inactive
Hiding the guide does not switch the CAD target
Layers remains open after returning to Paint
cases.exception: In a narrow phone layout scrolling the layer strip must reach the guide eye without closing CAD or blocking tools.

cases.title: Choose a paint layer when leaving CAD
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to choose a paint layer when leaving CAD, so I can separate parts of a picture and change one part without damaging the others.
steps: While CAD is open choose a normal paint sheet in Layers
Select Text and position a caption
criteria: Paint opens on the chosen sheet and Layers stays open
The caption is separate from the solid
Returning to CAD retains editable geometry
cases.exception: Closing CAD without picking a sheet must choose a valid paint target rather than direct raster painting into the solid preview.

cases.title: Restore the layer palette after Photo lab
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to restore the layer palette after Photo lab, so I can separate parts of a picture and change one part without damaging the others.
steps: Inspect the layer palette and target
criteria: Photo lab and layer controls do not compete for the same editing target
The prior useful palette state is restored
The active sheet and its saved adjustments remain coherent
cases.exception: Changing to basic mode hides advanced controls without deleting the layers or recipes they represent.

cases.title: Switch a painting into editable piece mode
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to switch a painting into editable piece mode, so I can keep individual parts adjustable as my illustration becomes more ambitious.
steps: Make raster marks then choose More Draw with Vectors
criteria: Existing paint remains visible and becomes addressable as intended
New vector geometry is a separate piece
Switching mode does not rescale the picture
cases.exception: Returning to Raster changes future drawing behavior without merging existing editable pieces.

cases.title: Create an independently editable shape
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to create an independently editable shape, so I can keep individual parts adjustable as my illustration becomes more ambitious.
steps: Draw a filled vector heart and an arrow
criteria: Each gesture creates a separate selectable shape
Resizing preserves its shape definition
The project retains editable geometry
cases.exception: An image export is allowed to rasterise its visible appearance but must not be mistaken for an editable project.

cases.title: Keep brush gestures separate as raster pieces
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to keep brush gestures separate as raster pieces, so I can keep individual parts adjustable as my illustration becomes more ambitious.
steps: Draw two brush gestures and one spray burst in Vectors mode
criteria: Raster gestures have their own cropped surfaces
Piece bounds follow the actual content
Neighbours do not move or merge
cases.exception: Transparent padding must not intercept clicks over a different visible piece unnecessarily.

cases.title: Keep text editable as a piece
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to keep text editable as a piece, so I can keep individual parts adjustable as my illustration becomes more ambitious.
steps: Create styled text in Vectors mode
Select move rotate and scale it
criteria: Text remains an individually editable scene item with its supported original text styling data
Transforms keep crisp geometry where applicable
Reopening retains its identity
cases.exception: Do not assume a general rich text editor exists: test only the text properties exposed by the app.

cases.title: Place stamps as editable artwork
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to place stamps as editable artwork, so I can keep individual parts adjustable as my illustration becomes more ambitious.
steps: Place two stamps in vector mode
criteria: Each stamp remains a separate supported piece
The chosen stamp and transform survive
Flipping one does not flip the other
cases.exception: Platform glyph differences must be recorded when comparing visual stamp appearance.

cases.title: Select one piece or a group
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to select one piece or a group, so I can keep individual parts adjustable as my illustration becomes more ambitious.
steps: Shift click another then remove it from selection
Drag a box around a group
criteria: Selection reflects the intended set
Group bounds enclose every selected piece
Later transforms apply only to that set
cases.exception: Blank paper clicks clear or settle selection according to the documented object interaction rule without deleting pieces.

cases.title: Reach a piece hidden behind another
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to reach a piece hidden behind another, so I can keep individual parts adjustable as my illustration becomes more ambitious.
steps: Select a named off paper item in the piece list
criteria: Each intended object can be reached
The selection indication names the actual target
The piece list can recover objects outside the visible paper
cases.exception: Transparent gaps and fully hidden pieces need a consistent hit testing rule rather than always selecting the top bounding box.

cases.title: Move precisely with arrows
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to move precisely with arrows, so I can keep individual parts adjustable as my illustration becomes more ambitious.
steps: Select a piece at a known coordinate
criteria: Ordinary arrows move by one paper pixel
Shift arrows move by ten
The document zoom does not change that distance
cases.exception: Typing arrows into a numeric field must change that field rather than moving the object behind it.

cases.title: Resize corners and sides accurately
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to resize corners and sides accurately, so I can keep individual parts adjustable as my illustration becomes more ambitious.
steps: Drag a corner and a side handle
criteria: Corner and side handles affect the intended dimensions
Shift preserves proportions where offered
The new bounds reflect the full transform
cases.exception: Handle crossing or zero dimension input must remain a valid object or be rejected without losing the original.

cases.title: Set exact position size and rotation
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to set exact position size and rotation, so I can keep individual parts adjustable as my illustration becomes more ambitious.
steps: Enter left -20 top 30 width 200 height 160 and a rotation
criteria: Numeric fields use paper pixels and degrees consistently
Negative positions remain valid
Other objects stay unchanged
cases.exception: Invalid empty infinite or singular values must not become saved transforms.

cases.title: Centre and arrange a group
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to centre and arrange a group, so I can keep individual parts adjustable as my illustration becomes more ambitious.
steps: Change stacking with forward backward front and back controls
criteria: The chosen group is centred by its bounds
Relative arrangement is preserved during a group move
Stacking changes only the intended objects
cases.exception: At the top or bottom of the order an unavailable arrange action must not duplicate or drop a piece.

cases.title: Duplicate a group without linking copies
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to duplicate a group without linking copies, so I can keep individual parts adjustable as my illustration becomes more ambitious.
steps: Select a group and duplicate it
criteria: The duplicate has equivalent content and separate identities
Moving the copy does not move the source
Undo removes or restores the operation coherently
cases.exception: Wet raster surfaces must not remain unintentionally shared between the duplicate and source.

cases.title: Copy and paste editable pieces
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to copy and paste editable pieces, so I can keep individual parts adjustable as my illustration becomes more ambitious.
criteria: Supported geometry and material data remain separate pieces
Relative placement within the group is retained
The system clipboard fallback is honest about raster versus editable content
cases.exception: Copying to an external application may use a PNG and must not be advertised as vector interchange.

cases.title: Apply a pixel effect to one piece
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to apply a pixel effect to one piece, so I can keep individual parts adjustable as my illustration becomes more ambitious.
steps: Select one raster or supported editable object
criteria: The selected content receives the intended effect
Unselected objects retain their data and pixels
The resulting object's editability is represented honestly
cases.exception: An unsupported object effect must be explained rather than flattening the whole layer as a hidden fallback.

cases.title: Preserve original raster detail while transforming
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to preserve original raster detail while transforming, so I can keep individual parts adjustable as my illustration becomes more ambitious.
steps: Insert a detailed image as a piece
criteria: Intermediate transforms reuse the retained original raster source
Detail is not repeatedly resampled
The final transform remains independently editable
cases.exception: Permanent off paper placement trimming has its separate documented retention rule and must be tested explicitly.

cases.title: Settle editable pieces on the desk
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to settle editable pieces on the desk, so I can keep individual parts adjustable as my illustration becomes more ambitious.
steps: Move an editable piece partly off paper
Click blank desk or press Escape
criteria: The documented deselection action places the editable piece
Its geometry remains recoverable according to piece kind
No new paint mark is created on the desk
cases.exception: Ordinary floating raster Cancel behavior is different and must not be substituted for this case.

cases.title: Keep materials and live ink on moved pieces
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to keep materials and live ink on moved pieces, so I can keep individual parts adjustable as my illustration becomes more ambitious.
steps: Create a live or textured piece
criteria: The material follows the object transform
Its clipping and alpha follow the transformed bounds
Unrelated live objects keep their behavior
cases.exception: Frozen still comparisons must use one captured time so animation phase is not mistaken for transform damage.

cases.title: Round trip a mixed scene
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to round trip a mixed scene, so I can keep individual parts adjustable as my illustration becomes more ambitious.
steps: Build shapes text stamps imported raster and Spiro objects
Save project and reopen in a fresh session
Edit one item of each kind
criteria: Piece kinds order transforms styling and supported source definitions survive
The composition matches at a controlled time
Editing each reopened item does not affect its neighbours
cases.exception: A malformed object in an external project must be rejected atomically without replacing the current scene.

cases.title: Open a photograph directly into Photo lab
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to open a photograph directly into Photo lab, so I can improve a photograph while keeping the original available for another try.
steps: Enable Advanced mode and choose Photo lab Open photo
Inspect the selected sheet and category
criteria: The chosen photo becomes the intended editing target
The lab reopens with useful remembered context
The import does not silently edit an old hidden layer
cases.exception: Cancelling the file chooser restores the previous draft and its settings rather than resetting the lab.

cases.title: Explore every photo adjustment group
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to explore every photo adjustment group, so I can improve a photograph while keeping the original available for another try.
steps: Browse Light Colour Curves Detail Effects and Geometry
Choose every group within each category
criteria: Controls are named and reachable
Current values survive category changes
Navigation alone does not change the photo
cases.exception: Short screens may use a combined group selector but every function must still be reachable.

cases.title: Compare Before and After without committing
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to compare Before and After without committing, so I can improve a photograph while keeping the original available for another try.
steps: Change exposure and saturation in a draft
criteria: Before shows the defined original source comparison
After restores the current draft preview
Comparison does not add an edit or replace the original
cases.exception: A comparison toggle during an asynchronous render must not show an old unrelated draft as the current result.

cases.title: Cancel only my current photo experiment
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to cancel only my current photo experiment, so I can improve a photograph while keeping the original available for another try.
steps: Reopen and make a very different draft
criteria: The earlier saved recipe remains
New draft changes are discarded
The original pixels and other sheets are unchanged
cases.exception: Photo lab Close and Escape must cancel the current draft, like Cancel. A late preview worker reply must not restore the discarded draft.

cases.title: Save editable photo adjustments with Done
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to save editable photo adjustments with Done, so I can improve a photograph while keeping the original available for another try.
steps: Reopen Photo lab and change them again
criteria: Done preserves the underlying original source
Reopening exposes the saved values
The next edit can revise the same recipe
cases.exception: A save or apply failure must leave the draft recoverable and must not report success before its commit completes.

cases.title: Undo a completed photo edit
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to undo a completed photo edit, so I can improve a photograph while keeping the original available for another try.
steps: Make a separate paint mark on another sheet
Undo the mark then the photo edit and Redo both
criteria: History restores the intended recipe at its own step
Painting remains separate
Redo reproduces the same rendered result at a fixed time
cases.exception: An open unsaved photo draft must not consume or corrupt the ordinary document Undo sequence.

cases.title: Reset one adjustment group
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to reset one adjustment group, so I can improve a photograph while keeping the original available for another try.
steps: Set values in Light and Colour
Reset only the current group with its reset control
criteria: Only that group's settings return to their defaults
Other adjustments remain
The preview and numeric values agree
cases.exception: Double clicking a single slider resets only that slider rather than the entire photo.

cases.title: Reset all saved photo adjustments
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to reset all saved photo adjustments, so I can improve a photograph while keeping the original available for another try.
steps: Reopen a photo with tone curves grain and lens corrections
criteria: All adjustment groups return to the defined defaults
The original remains available
The result can be undone
cases.exception: Cancel after Reset must restore the previously saved recipe rather than permanently clearing it.

cases.title: Increase exposure by a known stop
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to increase exposure by a known stop, so I can improve a photograph while keeping the original available for another try.
steps: Apply plus one EV then minus one EV on separate copies
criteria: Plus one EV doubles linear light before clipping and display encoding
Minus one halves it
Alpha stays unchanged
cases.exception: Do not expect displayed 8 bit sRGB values simply to double and do not use clipped white as the only sample.

cases.title: Raise brightness without confusing it with exposure
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to raise brightness without confusing it with exposure, so I can improve a photograph while keeping the original available for another try.
steps: Compare dark midtone and bright patches
criteria: The intended midtone brightness shift is visible
Neutral patches remain neutral
Reset restores the baseline recipe
cases.exception: Compare brightness and exposure as distinct controls rather than accepting either one for both cases.

cases.title: Add or soften contrast
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to add or soften contrast, so I can improve a photograph while keeping the original available for another try.
steps: Apply positive then negative contrast on fresh copies
criteria: Positive contrast increases useful tonal separation
Negative contrast softens it
The neutral baseline is recoverable
cases.exception: At extreme settings the preview must stay finite and alpha must not change even where RGB clips.

cases.title: Recover highlights and lift shadows
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to recover highlights and lift shadows, so I can improve a photograph while keeping the original available for another try.
steps: Reduce Highlights on a bright scene
Raise Shadows on a dark scene
criteria: Highlights primarily affect brighter tonal regions
Shadows primarily affect darker regions
The controls can be adjusted independently
cases.exception: Detail already clipped in the source must not be described as genuinely recovered information.

cases.title: Set white and black endpoints
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to set white and black endpoints, so I can improve a photograph while keeping the original available for another try.
steps: Inspect the histogram and known endpoint patches
criteria: Each endpoint control affects its intended tonal region
Clipping indicators respond to rendered values
Reset restores known baseline values
cases.exception: Nearly transparent or fully clear pixels must not dominate the clipping percentages.

cases.title: Try automatic tone adjustment
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to try automatic tone adjustment, so I can improve a photograph while keeping the original available for another try.
steps: Choose automatic tone on an unevenly exposed photo
criteria: The action produces a reproducible sensible tonal starting point
The controls show the resulting settings
Original pixels remain unchanged
cases.exception: An empty transparent image or constant colour image must not produce invalid numbers or an exception.

cases.title: Try every Photo look from one baseline
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to try every Photo look from one baseline, so I can improve a photograph while keeping the original available for another try.
steps: Choose Natural Punchy Black and white Warm film and Cool in different orders
criteria: Each look starts from the same pre look baseline
Switching order does not accumulate presets
Normal restores that baseline exactly
cases.exception: Every look must be tried and the saved baseline must include earlier manual edits rather than factory defaults.

cases.title: Know when a look becomes Custom
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to know when a look becomes Custom, so I can improve a photograph while keeping the original available for another try.
steps: Change a slider curve crop or automatic correction
Inspect the look selector then choose Normal
criteria: Each manual or automatic adjustment marks the look Custom
The preview represents the actual draft
Normal still restores the correct pre look baseline
cases.exception: A category change alone must not mark a look Custom.

cases.title: Read the histogram and clipping warnings
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to read the histogram and clipping warnings, so I can improve a photograph while keeping the original available for another try.
steps: Inspect a known distribution of opaque grey patches
Compare the histogram with independent pixel counts
criteria: Channel distributions describe the current rendered comparison
Shadow and highlight warnings follow defined thresholds
Fully transparent pixels are excluded
cases.exception: An empty image must give a defined zero count result without divide by zero or a false full clipping warning.

cases.title: Keep full size photo output consistent
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to keep full size photo output consistent, so I can improve a photograph while keeping the original available for another try.
steps: Make a fine detail edit on a large source
Save the recipe and export the full image
Inspect the same detail at source resolution
criteria: Output uses the full source rather than an enlarged preview cache
The saved recipe is honoured
Pixel dimensions follow the visible frame
cases.exception: A quick preview's lower detail is not acceptable evidence that the full size export has been verified.

cases.title: Keep photo settings after project reopen
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to keep photo settings after project reopen, so I can improve a photograph while keeping the original available for another try.
steps: Save a nondefault look baseline curves and crop in a project
Open it in a fresh session
criteria: All saved recipe values survive
Normal uses the saved baseline
Hidden crop margins remain available
cases.exception: Malformed external recipe values must reject the project atomically and preserve the open picture.

cases.title: Warm or cool a photograph
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to warm or cool a photograph, so I can make intentional colour choices and understand what changed.
steps: Move Temperature towards warm then cool on fresh copies
criteria: The controls produce opposite warm and cool shifts
The scene remains coherent
The original neutral setting can be restored
cases.exception: This is a relative RGB correction and must not be labelled or tested as camera RAW Kelvin recovery.

cases.title: Correct a green or magenta cast
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to correct a green or magenta cast, so I can make intentional colour choices and understand what changed.
steps: Compare a neutral patch and a skin coloured patch
criteria: The green to magenta direction agrees with the label
Temperature remains independently set
Alpha remains unchanged
cases.exception: Avoid accepting global desaturation as a successful tint correction.

cases.title: Choose a neutral point by sampling
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to choose a neutral point by sampling, so I can make intentional colour choices and understand what changed.
steps: Tap a known cast grey patch on the paper
criteria: The sample maps to the same source location in both views
The chosen neutral patch becomes more neutral
Sampling changes a recipe rather than painting a dot
cases.exception: Black clipped white fully transparent or outside image samples must be ignored or handled safely.

cases.title: Try automatic white balance
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to try automatic white balance, so I can make intentional colour choices and understand what changed.
steps: Apply automatic white balance to a photo with neutral samples
criteria: The algorithm returns finite bounded channel gains
The neutral cast is reduced on the designed fixture
The action is reversible
cases.exception: A strongly coloured artistic scene need not become objectively correct: Before and reset must remain available.

cases.title: Control saturation independently
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to control saturation independently, so I can make intentional colour choices and understand what changed.
steps: Set saturation to minus 100 then a positive value on separate copies
criteria: Minus 100 removes chroma while retaining tonal structure
Positive settings increase colour intensity within gamut
Neutral greys remain neutral
cases.exception: Alpha and clear margins must be preserved at both extremes.

cases.title: Use vibrance for a gentler colour boost
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to use vibrance for a gentler colour boost, so I can make intentional colour choices and understand what changed.
steps: Increase Vibrance on dull and already vivid patches
criteria: The boost follows the intended vibrance behavior
The two controls remain separately adjustable
The image is not recoloured by a hidden look change
cases.exception: Do not require a universal perceptual improvement on every photograph: use the defined colour fixture and bounded clipping observations.

cases.title: Shift hue around the colour wheel
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to shift hue around the colour wheel, so I can make intentional colour choices and understand what changed.
steps: Change Hue by a known angle on primary and secondary patches
criteria: Coloured patches rotate in the intended direction
Neutral samples remain neutral
The endpoints stay finite and consistent
cases.exception: A hue edit must not change alpha or swap the selected layer.

cases.title: Adjust each HSL colour range
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to adjust each HSL colour range, so I can make intentional colour choices and understand what changed.
steps: Choose each of Red Orange Yellow Green Aqua Blue Purple and Magenta
Change hue saturation and luminance separately
Compare target and non target samples
criteria: Every range can be selected and retains its own values
The targeted band changes more than distant hues
Transitions between bands remain smooth
cases.exception: Repeat near a hue boundary and across the red wrap so a seam or wrong range cannot hide in a single sample.

cases.title: Keep mixer settings independent
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to keep mixer settings independent, so I can make intentional colour choices and understand what changed.
steps: Set different values for red green and blue bands
criteria: Values do not leak from the previously displayed band
All eight range records survive
Reopening shows the correct range settings
cases.exception: Resetting the mixer group must not clear unrelated white balance or curves.

cases.title: Shape the RGB tone curve
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to shape the RGB tone curve, so I can make intentional colour choices and understand what changed.
steps: Add a midtone point to the RGB curve
criteria: The curve changes overall tone as shown
Neutral values remain neutral with no channel curve edits
The point and numeric fields agree
cases.exception: A point cannot cross its neighbours into unordered input positions.

cases.title: Edit red green and blue curves separately
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to edit red green and blue curves separately, so I can make intentional colour choices and understand what changed.
steps: Select each channel curve and adjust one interior point
criteria: The chosen channel changes without editing the other channel definitions
Channel selection is visible
Combined rendering honours all curves
cases.exception: A channel name change must not erase earlier points or apply the last edit to a different channel.

cases.title: Enter exact curve coordinates
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to enter exact curve coordinates, so I can make intentional colour choices and understand what changed.
steps: Compare the plotted point and exported neutral ramp
criteria: Displayed values map consistently to the curve's normalized domain
The point lies at the requested coordinates within display rounding
The output ramp follows the curve
cases.exception: Out of range or duplicate input positions must be constrained or rejected with the last valid curve retained.

cases.title: Move curve points by keyboard
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to move curve points by keyboard, so I can make intentional colour choices and understand what changed.
criteria: The chosen point alone moves in the expected axis
Keyboard and pointer editing share one curve definition
Delete removes only a removable interior point
cases.exception: Curve endpoints must remain present and ordered even when Delete or repeated arrows are used at a boundary.

cases.title: Try curve presets and reset them
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to try curve presets and reset them, so I can make intentional colour choices and understand what changed.
steps: Choose gentle S faded blacks and lifted shadows
criteria: Each preset has its named tonal character
The plotted curve represents the applied result
Reset returns the curves to their neutral line
cases.exception: A preset must replace its intended curve definition rather than silently accumulating additional points every time it is selected.

cases.title: Preserve smooth curves without ringing
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to preserve smooth curves without ringing, so I can make intentional colour choices and understand what changed.
steps: Create a steep but ordered multi point curve
criteria: Output remains bounded between valid channel limits
Interpolation does not invent severe overshoot around control points
The ramp has no artificial discontinuity
cases.exception: Repeated near neighbour points must not divide by zero or generate undefined pixels.

cases.title: Keep curve edits reversible in a photo draft
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to keep curve edits reversible in a photo draft, so I can make intentional colour choices and understand what changed.
steps: Save a recipe with a curve
criteria: The saved curve returns after cancellation
No draft point leaks into the saved recipe
Other adjustment groups retain their prior values
cases.exception: A late preview worker result from the cancelled draft must not overwrite the restored display.

cases.title: Keep colour alpha and hidden source separate
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to keep colour alpha and hidden source separate, so I can make intentional colour choices and understand what changed.
steps: Use a semitransparent colour patch and clear border
Apply mixer white balance and channel curves
criteria: Colour transforms operate on the intended RGB data
Alpha remains the original mask
Clear pixels stay visually clear
cases.exception: Inspect edge pixels over both black and white to expose colour fringes hidden by one background.

cases.title: Save a deliberately monochrome version
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to save a deliberately monochrome version, so I can make intentional colour choices and understand what changed.
steps: Choose Black and white then refine contrast and a curve
Reopen the project and choose Normal
criteria: PNG is the chosen finished monochrome image
The project still contains the colour source and pre look baseline
Normal can restore the intended earlier colour state
cases.exception: Importing the monochrome PNG is a new flattened image and cannot be accepted as proof of editable colour recovery.

cases.title: Sharpen real edges with amount radius and threshold
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to sharpen real edges with amount radius and threshold, so I can refine a photograph without mistaking display tricks for changes to its saved source.
steps: Increase Sharpness then vary Radius and Threshold separately
Inspect a line and a smooth patch
criteria: Amount controls strength and radius controls the neighbourhood scale
Threshold protects suitable low contrast areas
Source dimensions remain unchanged
cases.exception: High settings must remain bounded and should not inject colour into a fully transparent border.

cases.title: Separate texture and clarity
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to separate texture and clarity, so I can refine a photograph without mistaking display tricks for changes to its saved source.
steps: Change Texture then Clarity on separate copies
Inspect fine texture and broad local contrast
criteria: Both controls have their intended distinct scale of effect
Their values remain independent
Resetting one does not reset the other
cases.exception: The test must use fine and broad features so a duplicate implementation cannot pass both cases by looking merely sharper.

cases.title: Try Pop as a creative enhancement
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to try Pop as a creative enhancement, so I can refine a photograph without mistaking display tricks for changes to its saved source.
steps: Reset it and use manual controls instead
criteria: Pop produces its defined combined presence effect
Its amount is controllable and reversible
The app does not claim proprietary third party processing
cases.exception: A highly saturated photo may be less pleasing and must remain recoverable without accepting a subjective improvement as a test oracle.

cases.title: Remove or add haze deliberately
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to remove or add haze deliberately, so I can refine a photograph without mistaking display tricks for changes to its saved source.
steps: Use positive Dehaze on a hazy fixture
criteria: The directions have opposite atmospheric effects
The amount remains bounded
The original is still available
cases.exception: At extreme values no channel may become nonfinite and alpha must be preserved.

cases.title: Reduce luminance speckles
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to reduce luminance speckles, so I can refine a photograph without mistaking display tricks for changes to its saved source.
steps: Apply Luminance noise reduction to a seeded noisy grey patch beside a sharp edge
Compare local variance and edge position
criteria: Variance falls in the flat patch
The strong edge remains positioned correctly
Alpha and dimensions do not change
cases.exception: Do not use an already smooth image as the only proof that noise reduction works.

cases.title: Reduce coloured noise separately
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to reduce coloured noise separately, so I can refine a photograph without mistaking display tricks for changes to its saved source.
steps: Apply Colour noise reduction to seeded coloured speckles
criteria: Spurious chroma variation falls in the neutral patch
The control is independent from luminance smoothing
Large real colour boundaries remain identifiable
cases.exception: A uniform desaturation of the entire image is not an acceptable substitute for colour noise reduction.

cases.title: Frame a subject with a dark or light vignette
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to frame a subject with a dark or light vignette, so I can refine a photograph without mistaking display tricks for changes to its saved source.
steps: Apply negative and positive vignette settings on separate copies
criteria: The corners change in the labelled dark or light direction
The centre is relatively protected
The effect is stable after export
cases.exception: A cropped frame must use a consistent vignette coordinate policy rather than shifting unpredictably as panels open.

cases.title: Shape a vignette with its three controls
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to shape a vignette with its three controls, so I can refine a photograph without mistaking display tricks for changes to its saved source.
steps: Vary Midpoint Feather and Roundness one at a time
criteria: Midpoint changes reach
Feather changes transition softness
Roundness changes the contour while all remain independent
cases.exception: At all accepted endpoint values the effect must remain finite and within the picture bounds.

cases.title: Add deterministic film grain
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to add deterministic film grain, so I can refine a photograph without mistaking display tricks for changes to its saved source.
criteria: The grain pattern remains fixed for the same source and settings
Noise is achromatic as intended
The amount affects visible variation
cases.exception: A redraw or zoom must not regenerate a completely different random pattern.

cases.title: Change grain clump size and roughness
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to change grain clump size and roughness, so I can refine a photograph without mistaking display tricks for changes to its saved source.
steps: Use fixed Amount and vary Size then Roughness
Inspect spatial correlation and luminance regions
criteria: Size changes the texture's spatial scale
Roughness changes its structure
Grain preserves hue and alpha within the defined algorithm
cases.exception: Use seeded evidence and compare distributions instead of passing any two different random pictures.

cases.title: Crop by dragging a visible frame
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to crop by dragging a visible frame, so I can refine a photograph without mistaking display tricks for changes to its saved source.
steps: Drag a new box then move it from inside
Resize a corner and choose Done
criteria: The visible frame follows the selected source area
Moving preserves its size
Export uses the resulting visible extent
cases.exception: Corners cannot create a zero area or outside source frame and Cancel restores the previous crop.

cases.title: Crop with a fixed ratio
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to crop with a fixed ratio, so I can refine a photograph without mistaking display tricks for changes to its saved source.
criteria: The frame maintains the chosen ratio within pixel rounding
Its bounds stay inside the source
Switching back to free allows independent proportions
cases.exception: Both portrait and landscape source images must be checked so a fixed ratio cannot be accidentally inverted.

cases.title: Enter exact crop coordinates
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to enter exact crop coordinates, so I can refine a photograph without mistaking display tricks for changes to its saved source.
steps: Set x 100 y 50 width 200 height 100 on a 960 by 640 source
criteria: The output is 200 by 100 and begins at the intended source coordinate
Controls represent source pixels
Undo restores the prior shared frame
cases.exception: Negative outside zero or incompatible crop dimensions must be rejected without losing the saved frame.

cases.title: Use the phone preview to crop accurately
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to use the phone preview to crop accurately, so I can refine a photograph without mistaking display tricks for changes to its saved source.
steps: Open Geometry on a phone size view
Drag and resize the crop in the miniature
Compare it with the paper overlay
criteria: Miniature and full paper reference the same source rectangle
Letterboxing is accounted for
Touch interactions do not scroll the page instead of moving the crop
cases.exception: Touch outside the displayed image must not become an out of range source coordinate.

cases.title: Recover hidden crop margins later
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to recover hidden crop margins later, so I can refine a photograph without mistaking display tricks for changes to its saved source.
steps: Save a cropped recipe and project
Reopen Geometry in a fresh session
Expand the crop towards original edges
criteria: Full source margins are still available
Expanded content matches the original source
The project did not permanently trim the photo
cases.exception: The flattened exported PNG cannot restore hidden margins and must be kept distinct from the project during testing.

cases.title: Crop a multilayer composition consistently
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to crop a multilayer composition consistently, so I can refine a photograph without mistaking display tricks for changes to its saved source.
steps: Set a crop while editing one photo sheet
Export with a text sheet and another paint layer visible
criteria: The shared output frame applies consistently to every visible layer
Objects remain aligned
Each sheet retains its full source data
cases.exception: A local straighten or lens adjustment on one layer must not be mistaken for a global transformation of every layer.

cases.title: Straighten a horizon by drawing a line
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to straighten a horizon by drawing a line, so I can refine a photograph without mistaking display tricks for changes to its saved source.
steps: Drag along the sloping reference horizon on paper then miniature
criteria: The indicated horizon becomes level in the intended direction
The control reports its correction angle
Both input surfaces map consistently
cases.exception: A zero length or nearly vertical sample must have a defined safe response rather than a huge unexplained rotation.

cases.title: Straighten by an exact angle and fill the edges
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to straighten by an exact angle and fill the edges, so I can refine a photograph without mistaking display tricks for changes to its saved source.
steps: Enter an angle within minus 45 to plus 45 degrees
criteria: Angle and scale apply to the selected sheet
The chosen values are retained in the recipe
Increasing scale can intentionally cover transparent corners
cases.exception: A geometry preview must not permanently resize or trim the retained source pixels.

cases.title: Flip a photo sheet inside its frame
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to flip a photo sheet inside its frame, so I can refine a photograph without mistaking display tricks for changes to its saved source.
steps: Apply horizontal and vertical photo flips separately
criteria: The chosen sheet flips in the indicated direction
Other sheets and the shared frame remain aligned
Undo restores the recipe
cases.exception: Do not confuse Photo lab sheet flips with whole document Image flips.

cases.title: Correct vertical perspective
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to correct vertical perspective, so I can refine a photograph without mistaking display tricks for changes to its saved source.
steps: Use a fixture with converging vertical building lines
Adjust Vertical perspective with the grid visible
criteria: The intended vertical convergence changes in the expected direction
The grid offers a stable reference
The correction is retained without replacing the original
cases.exception: Extreme values must keep output finite and transparent outside samples safe.

cases.title: Correct horizontal perspective
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to correct horizontal perspective, so I can refine a photograph without mistaking display tricks for changes to its saved source.
steps: Compare with a vertical only correction
criteria: The horizontal control addresses the intended axis
It remains independent from vertical perspective
The frame and source remain coherent
cases.exception: Both positive and negative values must be exercised to expose reversed sign or swapped axes.

cases.title: Correct barrel or pincushion distortion
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to correct barrel or pincushion distortion, so I can refine a photograph without mistaking display tricks for changes to its saved source.
steps: Adjust lens distortion in each direction
criteria: The control produces the expected opposite radial warps
The result can be refined manually
The app does not promise automatic lens profile correction
cases.exception: Transparent borders and out of source samples must not wrap or produce opaque garbage.

cases.title: Align red and blue fringes
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to align red and blue fringes, so I can refine a photograph without mistaking display tricks for changes to its saved source.
steps: Use deliberately separated red and blue edge channels
criteria: The colour edge offsets change in the intended direction
Unrelated alpha stays intact
The value remains editable after save
cases.exception: A global hue shift or blur is not an acceptable substitute for spatial channel alignment.

cases.title: Combine photo geometry without stale previews
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to combine photo geometry without stale previews, so I can refine a photograph without mistaking display tricks for changes to its saved source.
steps: Change crop straighten perspective and lens settings rapidly
criteria: The final preview corresponds to the latest complete settings
Older worker responses cannot replace it
Full export uses that same saved recipe
cases.exception: Cancel during an unfinished preview must return to the prior saved state even if an old worker reply arrives later.

cases.title: Start a new picture at a chosen size
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to start a new picture at a chosen size, so I can keep independent copies and return to work with its intended editability intact.
steps: Choose New picture and enter supported dimensions
criteria: A valid ready document has the requested dimensions and defined initial paper
Old content is not mixed accidentally into the new one
The active target is valid
cases.exception: Invalid sizes must leave the previous document unchanged and explain the accepted limits.

cases.title: Open a supported image as a new picture
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to open a supported image as a new picture, so I can keep independent copies and return to work with its intended editability intact.
steps: Choose Open image and select each supported fixture format
criteria: The decoded source appears at the intended size
The working document targets that image
New marks align with its pixels
cases.exception: Cancelling the file picker retains the prior picture and corrupt data must be reported without partial replacement.

cases.title: Insert an image without replacing the drawing
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to insert an image without replacing the drawing, so I can keep independent copies and return to work with its intended editability intact.
steps: Choose Insert image and a small transparent PNG
Position it above the existing scene
criteria: Existing sheets remain intact
The inserted image becomes the supported movable content
Undo removes only the insertion
cases.exception: A very large inserted source must obey size limits without silently discarding the current picture.

cases.title: Paste a screenshot
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to paste a screenshot, so I can keep independent copies and return to work with its intended editability intact.
steps: Copy an image in another application
Choose Paste or the supported shortcut
criteria: A usable image arrives at the intended target
The app communicates clipboard restrictions honestly
Existing drawing remains
cases.exception: If browser permission is unavailable or clipboard contains only text the document must remain intact with an actionable message.

cases.title: Drop a picture onto the paper
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to drop a picture onto the paper, so I can keep independent copies and return to work with its intended editability intact.
steps: Drag a supported local image over the paper
criteria: The app inserts or opens it according to the visible drop contract
The browser does not navigate away to the file
The imported pixels can be positioned
cases.exception: Dropping an unsupported or corrupt file must not replace the document or leave a stuck drop overlay.

cases.title: Download the current PNG with Save
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to download the current PNG with Save, so I can keep independent copies and return to work with its intended editability intact.
steps: Decode the resulting PNG outside the app
criteria: File content and extension identify PNG
Dimensions equal the visible frame
Visible layers and supported adjustments appear correctly
cases.exception: Cursor handles rulers desk backgrounds and other editing overlays must not enter the exported pixels.

cases.title: Keep transparency in PNG WebP and TIFF
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to keep transparency in PNG WebP and TIFF, so I can keep independent copies and return to work with its intended editability intact.
steps: Hide Paper and export each alpha supporting format
criteria: Alpha is retained to the capability of each format
Opaque pixels keep their intended colours
Image dimensions are correct
cases.exception: Use an independent decoder and two contrasting backgrounds so a white flattening error cannot hide.

cases.title: Export JPEG and BMP with a white matte
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to export JPEG and BMP with a white matte, so I can keep independent copies and return to work with its intended editability intact.
steps: Hide Paper and export JPEG then BMP
Inspect transparent source areas in the files
criteria: The otherwise transparent region is composited onto white
The output uses the selected format
The editable project remains transparent
cases.exception: JPEG is lossy so use an agreed perceptual error threshold instead of demanding identical RGB bytes.

cases.title: Export a palette limited GIF honestly
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to export a palette limited GIF honestly, so I can keep independent copies and return to work with its intended editability intact.
steps: Export a colour rich image with clear and partial alpha areas as GIF
criteria: The file has no more than 256 palette colours
Transparency follows GIF's binary alpha limitation
The export is a still capture rather than an invented animated movie
cases.exception: Record quantisation loss explicitly and do not claim exact true colour or semitransparent GIF output.

cases.title: Import supported TIFF variants safely
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to import supported TIFF variants safely, so I can keep independent copies and return to work with its intended editability intact.
steps: Open uncompressed 8 bit RGB RGBA and greyscale TIFF fixtures
criteria: Supported variants decode accurately
Alpha is honoured for RGBA
Unsupported variants report their actual limitation
cases.exception: Malformed dimensions offsets or strip lengths must be rejected before memory use or partial document replacement.

cases.title: Name a saved file predictably
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to name a saved file predictably, so I can keep independent copies and return to work with its intended editability intact.
steps: Enter a descriptive name with an existing image extension
Repeat with reserved filename characters and an empty name
criteria: The resulting extension matches the chosen format
Invalid filename characters are made safe
The fallback name is usable
cases.exception: The name must not acquire duplicated misleading extensions such as picture.png.jpg unintentionally.

cases.title: Print the visible finished picture
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to print the visible finished picture, so I can keep independent copies and return to work with its intended editability intact.
steps: Choose Print on a cropped multilayer image
criteria: The preview contains the finished composition at the correct aspect ratio
Editing overlays are absent
Cancelling print leaves the document unchanged
cases.exception: Actual printer output and printer settings are external integration checks rather than a success inferred from opening print preview.

cases.title: Save an independent editable project
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to save an independent editable project, so I can keep independent copies and return to work with its intended editability intact.
steps: Save a project with layers objects recipes and live ink
Retain the actual downloaded bytes and checksum
Open the file in a fresh app session
criteria: The file identifies a supported RetroPaint project
All supported editing definitions survive
The reconstructed composition matches at a controlled time
cases.exception: A plain PNG renamed with a project extension must not pass project validation.

cases.title: Reopen a project through the real file input
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to reopen a project through the real file input, so I can keep independent copies and return to work with its intended editability intact.
steps: Close any active feature or photo draft deliberately
criteria: The file chooser pathway loads the intended file
Layer order target camera and recipes are restored
Each type of content can be edited afterward
cases.exception: Calling a serializer and parser directly is useful supplementary coverage but does not substitute for this user workflow.

cases.title: Read earlier project versions
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to read earlier project versions, so I can keep independent copies and return to work with its intended editability intact.
steps: Open each available supported legacy project fixture
Save it as a new project
criteria: Earlier supported data remains visible and editable to its documented capability
Missing newer settings receive safe defaults
Resaving preserves the migrated picture
cases.exception: An unknown future project version must be explained rather than accepted with silently discarded fields.

cases.title: Reject a damaged project atomically
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to reject a damaged project atomically, so I can keep independent copies and return to work with its intended editability intact.
steps: Keep a named unsaved picture open
Try truncated JSON malformed images invalid IDs singular transforms and bad recipes
criteria: The current document remains unchanged after every rejection
The message identifies an actionable format problem
No partial layers become active
cases.exception: A valid opening immediately after a rejection must work so the failure cannot poison future imports.

cases.title: Save a stable snapshot while encoding
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to save a stable snapshot while encoding, so I can keep independent copies and return to work with its intended editability intact.
steps: Begin saving a large editable project
Make a clearly different edit after snapshot capture if controls allow it
criteria: The file represents one coherent captured state
Later edits do not leak into some encoded sheets only
The working document keeps the later edit
cases.exception: Do not require a particular timing shortcut: capture a deterministic test seam and record when the snapshot was taken.

cases.title: Keep Save usable after a failed export
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to keep Save usable after a failed export, so I can keep independent copies and return to work with its intended editability intact.
steps: Cause an unsupported codec or resource failure in a disposable session
Retry a small PNG or project
criteria: The failed action does not claim a successful file
Busy controls become usable again
Retry can produce a valid independently decoded file
cases.exception: Repeated rapid Save presses must not launch an unbounded set of duplicate encoding jobs.

cases.title: Recover a draft after a refresh
cases.story: As a beginning young artist, I want to recover a draft after a refresh, so I can keep independent copies and return to work with its intended editability intact.
steps: Make settled edits and allow draft saving to finish
criteria: The recovered picture includes supported layers objects live data and recipes
The prompt does not block a ready new canvas
The chosen draft is identified
cases.exception: An unsaved active gesture text draft or photo draft must not be mistaken for a safely settled recovery checkpoint.

cases.title: Choose among recent drafts
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to choose among recent drafts, so I can keep independent copies and return to work with its intended editability intact.
steps: Page through previews and restore a chosen one
criteria: The correct name size and preview identify each entry
Pagination reaches all retained drafts
Restoring chooses the requested complete picture
cases.exception: A missing or damaged stored entry must report failure without replacing the current drawing with an empty picture.

cases.title: Undo a draft restore
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to undo a draft restore, so I can keep independent copies and return to work with its intended editability intact.
criteria: The earlier unsaved document returns with its editable content
Redo can return to the restored draft
The draft store remains independent
cases.exception: Recovery must not reset the history to a state from which the pre restore work is irretrievable.

cases.title: Keep duplicated browser tabs independent
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to keep duplicated browser tabs independent, so I can keep independent copies and return to work with its intended editability intact.
steps: Make different settled edits in both
Refresh and inspect recovery in each
criteria: Separate working identities protect each evolving picture
One tab does not overwrite the other's recovery data
Both can save independent project files
cases.exception: This is not simultaneous shared collaboration and no real time multiuser synchronization is implied.

cases.title: Handle unavailable browser storage honestly
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to handle unavailable browser storage honestly, so I can keep independent copies and return to work with its intended editability intact.
steps: Run with IndexedDB or preference storage unavailable
criteria: Painting remains usable
The app does not falsely claim a browser draft is safely stored
Independent file saving remains offered
cases.exception: Quota or blocked database errors must not repeatedly interrupt every stroke or destroy the active document.

cases.title: Respect draft retention and large document limits
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to respect draft retention and large document limits, so I can keep independent copies and return to work with its intended editability intact.
steps: Create more than eight recovery candidates within a disposable database
Try a picture beyond automatic draft eligibility
criteria: Retention follows the defined count and storage budget
The newest valid working draft is protected as designed
Oversized work is directed to Save project
cases.exception: The 24 million stored pixel and 50 million serialized character draft cutoffs are distinct from the ordinary image and layer limits.

cases.title: Open enhancement on a finished composition
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to open enhancement on a finished composition, so I can judge generated detail before keeping a larger copy of my work.
steps: Enable Advanced mode and choose Super resolution
criteria: The source includes visible layers photo adjustments and the shared crop
The source dimensions are clear
Opening and closing do not alter the document
cases.exception: A hidden reference sheet must not unexpectedly appear in the enhancement source.

cases.title: Choose exactly double or quadruple size
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to choose exactly double or quadruple size, so I can judge generated detail before keeping a larger copy of my work.
steps: Select 2 times then 4 times on a known 160 by 120 input
criteria: The choices produce 320 by 240 and 640 by 480 respectively
The selected scale is visible
The editable original stays 160 by 120
cases.exception: Unsupported scale values are rejected and an output edge above 16384 requires a clear alternative.

cases.title: Choose a representative preview detail
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to choose a representative preview detail, so I can judge generated detail before keeping a larger copy of my work.
steps: Move the yellow area by clicking then dragging
criteria: The selected source area is consistent between overview Before and Enhanced
The area stays inside the source
Each listed size is usable within smaller images
cases.exception: A click in overview letterboxing must not select an unrelated or invalid source rectangle.

cases.title: Move the preview area with the keyboard
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to move the preview area with the keyboard, so I can judge generated detail before keeping a larger copy of my work.
steps: Use arrow keys then Shift arrows
criteria: Arrows move by the defined 8 source pixels and Shift arrows by 32
Clamping retains a valid region
The new selection invalidates an obsolete result appropriately
cases.exception: At source boundaries repeated keys must not wrap the selection to the opposite corner.

cases.title: Compare original and generated detail
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to compare original and generated detail, so I can judge generated detail before keeping a larger copy of my work.
criteria: Both views show the same source region at comparable presentation size
The labels state which is shown
The user can reject invented or degraded detail
cases.exception: A larger interpolated source presented as the neural result is not acceptable evidence of enhancement.

cases.title: Enhance the whole image and save it
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to enhance the whole image and save it, so I can judge generated detail before keeping a larger copy of my work.
steps: Save enhanced PNG and decode it independently
criteria: The complete visible composition is processed
The final PNG has the selected output dimensions
The original editable project remains intact
cases.exception: The successful preview tile must not be passed off as a completed whole image result.

cases.title: Keep transparent margins clean
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to keep transparent margins clean, so I can judge generated detail before keeping a larger copy of my work.
steps: Enhance a semitransparent coloured object with clear padding
criteria: Clear pixels stay clear
Alpha is resampled separately as designed
Coloured edges avoid black contamination from transparent RGB padding
cases.exception: Inspect all four margins and tile boundaries rather than one opaque centre patch.

cases.title: Avoid seams between processed tiles
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to avoid seams between processed tiles, so I can judge generated detail before keeping a larger copy of my work.
steps: Enhance a grid and continuous gradient crossing tile boundaries
Compare boundary bands with nearby bands
criteria: There are no systematic seam lines or repeated edge strips
The output covers the whole source once
Mirrored border handling is coherent at outer edges
cases.exception: A tile progress counter alone cannot establish that every output row was written correctly.

cases.title: Cancel during model loading or processing
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to cancel during model loading or processing, so I can judge generated detail before keeping a larger copy of my work.
criteria: Cancellation returns control promptly
No stale completion reopens the closed dialog
The editable source remains unchanged
cases.exception: A later new enhancement job must not receive progress or output from the cancelled job.

cases.title: Run with a CPU fallback when needed
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to run with a CPU fallback when needed, so I can judge generated detail before keeping a larger copy of my work.
steps: Use a disposable environment without worker WebGL
Compare with the supported network result tolerance
criteria: The same model family can run on CPU
Progress and cancel remain usable
The app reports a useful failure if neither path can run
cases.exception: Do not silently replace neural inference with a different filter and label it the same result.

cases.title: Load enhancement assets locally and on demand
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to load enhancement assets locally and on demand, so I can judge generated detail before keeping a larger copy of my work.
steps: Open the app without starting enhancement
Start enhancement once with a local source
criteria: Large model resources are deferred until needed
Models are requested from the app origin
No image payload is uploaded to an external service
cases.exception: A blocked or missing model download must preserve the picture and offer a recoverable retry rather than freeze the editor.

cases.title: Process supported large sources without a fake cap
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to process supported large sources without a fake cap, so I can judge generated detail before keeping a larger copy of my work.
steps: Choose valid input near supported image limits
Request both supported scales in a controlled resource test
criteria: Accepted output respects the 16384 pixel edge limit
Row band streaming can finish without requiring a giant export canvas
The old arbitrary 32 megapixel restriction does not block an otherwise supported job
cases.exception: Resource failure must be reported honestly with cancellation or retry and must never damage the original project.

cases.title: Enter and leave the 3D workshop safely
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to enter and leave the 3D workshop safely, so I can turn a simple idea into an accurately placed editable solid.
criteria: The workshop opens without replacing the drawing
Its controls use millimetres
Returning gives a valid paint sheet and retains the solid document
cases.exception: Opening twice must reuse the current workshop rather than create duplicate canvases or an extra 3D layer.

cases.title: Build with every starting primitive
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to build with every starting primitive, so I can turn a simple idea into an accurately placed editable solid.
steps: Add Cube Sphere Cylinder Cone Torus Tube Pyramid and Wedge in separate setups
criteria: Every listed shape has its recognisable solid form
The piece is in the active 3D layer
Adding it is one reversible operation
cases.exception: A collapsed or invalid primitive must be rejected rather than committed as an empty printable model.

cases.title: Understand the bed and model units
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to understand the bed and model units, so I can turn a simple idea into an accurately placed editable solid.
steps: Create a 20 by 20 by 20 mm cube
Compare it with the bed grid
criteria: Bounds remain 20 mm on each local axis
Volume is 8000 cubic mm for an unmodified cube
Camera zoom does not change those values
cases.exception: The default bed drawing is a reference and must not be confused with an automatic printer fit guarantee.

cases.title: Select a piece and multiple pieces
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to select a piece and multiple pieces, so I can turn a simple idea into an accurately placed editable solid.
steps: Click one solid then Shift click another
criteria: The selected set is visibly marked
Multiple selection contains the intended unique IDs
Blank selection does not delete geometry
cases.exception: Hidden or locked pieces follow explicit selection and editability rules rather than accidentally becoming editable.

cases.title: Move a solid with its coloured handle
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to move a solid with its coloured handle, so I can turn a simple idea into an accurately placed editable solid.
steps: Drag one axis handle across several grid intervals
criteria: Only the intended axis changes
The gesture stays active across history updates
One Undo restores the original position
cases.exception: Losing pointer capture mid drag must end in a coherent committed or cancelled move without a stuck gizmo.

cases.title: Enter exact position and rotation
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to enter exact position and rotation, so I can turn a simple idea into an accurately placed editable solid.
steps: Set position to -12.5 4 and 10 mm and Z rotation to 30 degrees
criteria: Fields and piece transform agree
The model's world bounds reflect the transform
The original dimensions are unchanged
cases.exception: Blank nonfinite or out of range coordinates must not replace the last valid transform.

cases.title: Turn a piece with rotation rings
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to turn a piece with rotation rings, so I can turn a simple idea into an accurately placed editable solid.
criteria: The chosen axis rotates around the intended pivot
Snap increments match the control
One gesture is one reversible transform
cases.exception: Use an asymmetric piece so a wrong axis rotation cannot pass through visual symmetry.

cases.title: Resize with handles and exact dimensions
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to resize with handles and exact dimensions, so I can turn a simple idea into an accurately placed editable solid.
steps: Resize one local axis with its handle
Enter exact local width depth and height
criteria: The local dimensions reach the requested values
Body placement follows the defined anchor
Other selected pieces follow the documented multi selection rule
cases.exception: Zero or negative dimensions and singular scale must be rejected before they become saved geometry.

cases.title: Keep proportions when resizing
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to keep proportions when resizing, so I can turn a simple idea into an accurately placed editable solid.
steps: Enable Keep proportions and set width 40
criteria: Proportional resize produces 40 by 20 by 60 within geometric tolerance
Free mode changes only requested axes
The control state is visible
cases.exception: Nonuniform pre existing scale must not unexpectedly compound dimensions twice.

cases.title: Set a tube wall within its size
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to set a tube wall within its size, so I can turn a simple idea into an accurately placed editable solid.
steps: Create a tube with known outer diameter and height
criteria: The wall matches the entered thickness within tessellation tolerance
The central bore remains open
The outside dimensions remain as requested
cases.exception: A wall that closes or inverts the bore must be constrained or rejected with the intact original retained.

cases.title: Name and colour a solid
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to name and colour a solid, so I can turn a simple idea into an accurately placed editable solid.
steps: Rename one piece and choose each palette colour plus a custom colour
criteria: The body name and colour remain attached to its identity
Colour selection affects only intended pieces
The project retains colours
cases.exception: STL is a geometry format and must not be accepted as proof that body colours survived an export.

cases.title: Duplicate a solid independently
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to duplicate a solid independently, so I can turn a simple idea into an accurately placed editable solid.
criteria: The copy has its own unique identity
Its source recipe starts equivalent
Editing its transform does not mutate the original
cases.exception: Copying a feature tree must not introduce duplicate child IDs that break later History editing.

cases.title: Delete an unlocked piece and recover it
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to delete an unlocked piece and recover it, so I can turn a simple idea into an accurately placed editable solid.
steps: Select an unlocked piece among several
criteria: Only the intended piece is removed
Undo restores its complete recipe and transform
Redo repeats the same deletion
cases.exception: Locked pieces must be protected and an empty selection must not delete the whole layer.

cases.title: Hide and lock individual pieces
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to hide and lock individual pieces, so I can turn a simple idea into an accurately placed editable solid.
steps: Hide one piece and lock another
Try transforms then restore visibility and unlock
criteria: Hidden geometry is absent from the intended display and export scopes
Locked geometry cannot be changed accidentally
Restoring state retains recipes
cases.exception: The normal picture layer eye and the piece eye are different scopes and must both be tested.

cases.title: Create and switch 3D layers
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to create and switch 3D layers, so I can turn a simple idea into an accurately placed editable solid.
steps: Switch between layers and select pieces
criteria: The active layer is named
Pieces remain in their owning layer
Ordinary paint sheets are not converted into CAD layers silently
cases.exception: Layer count and total document limits still apply when adding a CAD layer.

cases.title: Move pieces to a different 3D layer
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to move pieces to a different 3D layer, so I can turn a simple idea into an accurately placed editable solid.
criteria: Pieces arrive once with their transforms and recipes
The destination becomes a coherent editing target
Undo restores their original ownership
cases.exception: A full destination layer or selecting the same source and destination must fail safely without duplication or loss.

cases.title: Snap movement and angles deliberately
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to snap movement and angles deliberately, so I can turn a simple idea into an accurately placed editable solid.
steps: Choose each offered grid and angle increment
Drag a piece and a rotation ring
criteria: Transforms follow the selected increments while snapping is enabled
Free movement is available when disabled
The numeric result matches the visible controls
cases.exception: Boundary values and negative coordinates must round consistently rather than drifting on repeated moves.

cases.title: Put a piece on the bed and centre it
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to put a piece on the bed and centre it, so I can turn a simple idea into an accurately placed editable solid.
steps: Move a rotated solid partly below Z zero
criteria: The world minimum Z reaches zero
Rotation and dimensions stay unchanged
Centering uses the intended world bounds
cases.exception: A rotated or scaled piece must not use untransformed local bounds and remain partly under the bed.

cases.title: Align two pieces accurately
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to align two pieces accurately, so I can turn a simple idea into an accurately placed editable solid.
steps: Choose a target and a moving piece
Try each offered axis and before centre after placement mode with a known gap
criteria: The target stays fixed
The moving piece reaches the requested relation using world bounds
Gap sign and units are consistent
cases.exception: An invalid target or one locked moving piece must be explained without partly transforming the selected group.

cases.title: Mate two opposite faces
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to mate two opposite faces, so I can turn a simple idea into an accurately placed editable solid.
steps: Pick a face on the moving solid and a face on the target
criteria: The chosen faces become coincident in the requested relation
Their normals oppose as intended
One Undo restores the moving solid
cases.exception: An ambiguous unsupported or identical face pair must not create a random rotation or alter the target.

cases.title: Repeat pieces in rows and around an axis
