cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to repeat pieces in rows and around an axis, so I can turn a simple idea into an accurately placed editable solid.
steps: Use the available linear and radial repeat controls
Enter count spacing and turn values
criteria: The intended number of independent copies is created
Positions or angles follow the entered series
The original stays present
cases.exception: Counts that exceed layer capacity must fail before producing a partial pattern.

cases.title: Mirror a solid without turning it inside out
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to mirror a solid without turning it inside out, so I can turn a simple idea into an accurately placed editable solid.
steps: Choose each offered mirror axis on an asymmetric solid
criteria: The mirrored shape has the intended handedness
Its surface remains outward and closed
Volume magnitude is preserved
cases.exception: A negative transform determinant must not yield an inward STL or erase a cavity during later repair.

cases.title: Sketch on every fixed workplane
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to sketch on every fixed workplane, so I can describe a shape by its dimensions and make predictable additions and cuts.
steps: Choose Floor XY Front XZ and Side YZ
Draw the same rectangle on each
Pull it by a known amount
criteria: The plane basis and pull direction match the selected view
Dimensions are measured in millimetres
Each result is a closed correctly oriented solid
cases.exception: Changing plane during an unfinished sketch must not commit points in a mixed coordinate system.

cases.title: Draw dimensioned rectangles and circles
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to draw dimensioned rectangles and circles, so I can describe a shape by its dimensions and make predictable additions and cuts.
steps: Enter rectangle start width and height
Create a separate circle by centre and diameter
criteria: The rectangle bounds match its entered coordinates
The circle's size follows its diameter controls
The pulled shapes retain editable sketch definitions
cases.exception: A circle starts from its centre and must not be mistakenly positioned from a corner like a rectangle.

cases.title: Draw and finish a custom polygon sketch
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to draw and finish a custom polygon sketch, so I can describe a shape by its dimensions and make predictable additions and cuts.
steps: Finish with the supported control or Enter
criteria: The selected points remain in order
The completed profile closes once
The resulting solid has the intended concavity
cases.exception: Too few distinct points collinear points or self intersections must give a clear safe failure or supported defined result.

cases.title: Pick a whole flat support face
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to pick a whole flat support face, so I can describe a shape by its dimensions and make predictable additions and cuts.
steps: Select a cube and choose Pick flat face
Tap its top face then draw a sketch
criteria: The entire geometric support face is identified
The sketch lies on it in world space
Orbiting is distinct from adding a point
cases.exception: Curved faces or tessellation diagonals must not masquerade as supported flat sketch planes.

cases.title: Pull a sketch into a new solid
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to pull a sketch into a new solid, so I can describe a shape by its dimensions and make predictable additions and cuts.
steps: Create a 10 by 10 rectangle on XY
Set pull to 30 and New piece
criteria: The result spans Z zero through 30 with volume 3000 cubic mm
The recipe retains the input outline and pull
Undo removes one created feature
cases.exception: Zero pull and invalid numeric input must leave the last valid sketch usable.

cases.title: Pull in the negative direction
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to pull in the negative direction, so I can describe a shape by its dimensions and make predictable additions and cuts.
steps: Create the same rectangle on XY
Pull by -10 as a new piece
criteria: The result extends to Z -10 without an unintended positive extension
Volume magnitude is 1000 cubic mm
Surface orientation is outward
cases.exception: Negative pull must not invert triangle winding or reverse an attached face reference unexpectedly.

cases.title: Join a fixed plane pull with exact endpoints
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to join a fixed plane pull with exact endpoints, so I can describe a shape by its dimensions and make predictable additions and cuts.
steps: Use the 10 by 10 sketch on XY through the cube
Join with pull 30 then -10 in separate copies
criteria: Positive result has Z zero to 30 and volume 9000 cubic mm
Negative result has Z -10 to 20 and volume 9000 cubic mm
History retains the exact entered pull
cases.exception: A robustness overlap allowance must not add 0.02 mm to the far endpoint or alter the requested overall size.

cases.title: Cut a dimensioned recess
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to cut a dimensioned recess, so I can describe a shape by its dimensions and make predictable additions and cuts.
steps: Sketch a centred 10 by 10 rectangle on a cube face
criteria: The recess floor is 5 mm below its support face
The outside size is unchanged
Removed volume is 500 cubic mm for the simple fixture
cases.exception: The cut must not pass through the whole body or extend beyond the requested depth because of contact tolerances.

cases.title: Cut all the way through
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to cut all the way through, so I can describe a shape by its dimensions and make predictable additions and cuts.
steps: Sketch a circular hole on a solid face
Increase the source body's depth through History
criteria: The opening reaches both intended sides
The downstream cut rebuilds for the new depth
The original hole sketch remains editable
cases.exception: A changed support face that cannot be resolved must stop rebuilding rather than cut in an arbitrary plane.

cases.title: Join a sketch on a picked face
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to join a sketch on a picked face, so I can describe a shape by its dimensions and make predictable additions and cuts.
steps: Pick a flat face of a transformed cube
Join with a known positive height
criteria: The pad grows from that support face
Any inward contact allowance preserves the far endpoint
The result is one valid joined solid
cases.exception: Repeat on opposite faces and after source size changes so a hard coded world Z assumption cannot pass.

cases.title: Taper and twist an extrusion
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to taper and twist an extrusion, so I can describe a shape by its dimensions and make predictable additions and cuts.
steps: Pull an asymmetric sketch with Top size multiplier then Twist
criteria: Taper changes top profile size relative to bottom
Twist turns the profile through the specified angle
Neutral settings reproduce the untapered untwisted case
cases.exception: Collapsed tapered tops self intersections or unsupported precision operations must fail with the original retained.

cases.title: Revolve a predefined profile
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to revolve a predefined profile, so I can describe a shape by its dimensions and make predictable additions and cuts.
steps: Choose Hollow vase Goblet and Knob profiles in separate setups
criteria: Each preset makes its intended closed solid
Hollow profiles contain real empty space
The profile remains accessible in History
cases.exception: A displayed silhouette alone cannot prove that the central cavity exists in exported geometry.

cases.title: Draw a custom revolve profile
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to draw a custom revolve profile, so I can describe a shape by its dimensions and make predictable additions and cuts.
steps: Add and drag radius height points
Edit the coordinate list and finish
criteria: Profile points and numeric list agree
Radius stays on the supported side of the axis
The revolved result uses the intended profile
cases.exception: Duplicate points self intersections negative radius or a profile on the axis must be rejected or constrained safely.

cases.title: Make a partial revolution
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to make a partial revolution, so I can describe a shape by its dimensions and make predictable additions and cuts.
steps: Revolve a known annular profile by 180 degrees
criteria: The partial solid has closed end faces
Its volume follows the chosen fraction of the analytic full revolution
Editing retains its axis and profile
cases.exception: Near zero or invalid angles must not produce an open broken printable mesh.

cases.title: Join subtract intersect and wrap solids
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to join subtract intersect and wrap solids, so I can describe a shape by its dimensions and make predictable additions and cuts.
steps: Use overlapping cubes and a separate cutter
Perform Join Subtract Keep overlap and Wrap with hull on independent copies
criteria: Join removes internal overlap
Subtract retains the named target and removes cutter volume
Intersection and Hull have their respective analytic expected bounds and volume
On the separate gapped cube fixture, Hull fills the gap and has volume 3000 cubic mm, while Union retains the two components with volume 2000 cubic mm
cases.exception: Select at least two supported pieces and test target order so commutative Join cannot conceal a reversed subtraction.

cases.title: Keep boolean source pieces editable
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to keep boolean source pieces editable, so I can describe a shape by its dimensions and make predictable additions and cuts.
steps: Join or subtract two named primitives
Change an original size and apply
criteria: Source definitions remain nested in the result
Later geometry rebuilds from the changed input
Undo restores one complete edit
cases.exception: A failed rebuild must keep the previous final solid and the draft inputs rather than replacing them with a partial tree.

cases.title: Add a driving line length
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to add a driving line length, so I can describe a shape by its dimensions and make predictable additions and cuts.
steps: Select a numbered line and add a length dimension
criteria: The line reaches the entered millimetre length within solver tolerance
The definition is saved
Dependent solid geometry rebuilds
cases.exception: An impossible length combined with existing relations must retain the last valid sketch and explain the conflict.

cases.title: Constrain horizontal and vertical lines
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to constrain horizontal and vertical lines, so I can describe a shape by its dimensions and make predictable additions and cuts.
criteria: The constrained directions remain horizontal or vertical in the sketch plane
Other free points can still move
The controls identify the active relations
cases.exception: Redundant or conflicting relations must not cause a jump to an unrelated far away configuration.

cases.title: Control line angles and relations
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to control line angles and relations, so I can describe a shape by its dimensions and make predictable additions and cuts.
steps: Prepare separate valid sketches for angle to X, parallel, perpendicular and angle between two lines
Select the appropriate numbered lines and add each requested relation
Edit each supported angle value and rebuild the solid to inspect its geometry
criteria: Each relation solves its stated geometric condition
Angle between directed lines uses the declared 0 to 180 degree convention
Stored relations survive reopening
cases.exception: Selecting the same line twice or an invalid line index must be rejected without altering the sketch.

cases.title: Dimension a circle by diameter
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to dimension a circle by diameter, so I can describe a shape by its dimensions and make predictable additions and cuts.
steps: Draw an elliptical circle type outline
Add a diameter dimension and edit it
criteria: The diameter constraint produces a round section
Its physical diameter matches the entered value
The solid updates from the constrained outline
cases.exception: A polygon cannot acquire an unsupported circle diameter relation through stale controls.

cases.title: Edit remove and persist constraints
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to edit remove and persist constraints, so I can describe a shape by its dimensions and make predictable additions and cuts.
steps: Edit one via its label and remove another
criteria: Labels and selectors refer to the same definitions
Removing a relation frees the intended degree of freedom
The reopened constraints still drive geometry
cases.exception: A decorative annotation that does not change rebuilt geometry must fail this case.

cases.title: Reject conflicting dimensions without losing a sketch
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to reject conflicting dimensions without losing a sketch, so I can describe a shape by its dimensions and make predictable additions and cuts.
steps: Request an incompatible extra angle or length
criteria: The last valid geometry stays visible and saved
The message identifies a conflict
The draft can be corrected without restarting the whole model
cases.exception: Do not accept silently deleting an existing constraint or relaxing the requested tolerance as a successful solve.

cases.title: Read and name the construction tree
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to read and name the construction tree, so I can refine an earlier design and preserve its construction instead of rebuilding it from scratch.
steps: Build a primitive plus a cut and finish
Open History and expand each step
criteria: The tree exposes original inputs and operation order
The selected node corresponds to its source
Names survive save and reopen
cases.exception: Pagination must not omit hidden branches or confuse tree node identity after a rename.

cases.title: Preview an earlier dimension change
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to preview an earlier dimension change, so I can refine an earlier design and preserve its construction instead of rebuilding it from scratch.
steps: Select an original source sketch or primitive
Compare saved project data before Apply
criteria: The workbench shows a rebuilt final result
Later supported features follow the edit
The saved document remains unchanged during Preview
cases.exception: An invalid preview stays in the editor with an explanation and the previous saved solid intact.

cases.title: Apply one history edit atomically
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to apply one history edit atomically, so I can refine an earlier design and preserve its construction instead of rebuilding it from scratch.
criteria: Apply produces the complete rebuilt result
One Undo returns the complete earlier model
Redo restores the applied result and feature data
cases.exception: The history must not contain separate intermediate states for every slider or preview rebuild.

cases.title: Cancel a feature draft completely
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to cancel a feature draft completely, so I can refine an earlier design and preserve its construction instead of rebuilding it from scratch.
steps: Compare saved data and mesh with the baseline
criteria: The original recipe is unchanged
The original final geometry returns
Draft helper outlines and pink edit overlays disappear
cases.exception: A worker response that arrives after cancellation must not commit or redisplay the cancelled edit.

cases.title: Suppress and enable a build feature
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to suppress and enable a build feature, so I can refine an earlier design and preserve its construction instead of rebuilding it from scratch.
steps: Suppress a cut or shell step
criteria: Suppression retains the original feature definition
Its documented target passes through to later supported steps
Reenabling rebuilds the intended final model
cases.exception: Suppressing a required support may cause a clear rebuild error and must not fabricate a substitute face.

cases.title: Inspect earlier geometry on the timeline
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to inspect earlier geometry on the timeline, so I can refine an earlier design and preserve its construction instead of rebuilding it from scratch.
steps: Select each build step and move the playhead
criteria: Earlier geometry is temporary inspection
Latest restores the full solid
The project recipe never becomes the preview result
cases.exception: Construction and export while rolled back must require Latest or explain the restriction rather than save the wrong step.

cases.title: Keep timeline and tree navigation reachable
cases.story: As an adventurous older child, I want to keep timeline and tree navigation reachable, so I can refine an earlier design and preserve its construction instead of rebuilding it from scratch.
steps: Build enough steps to require pagination
Reach the first middle and last steps in tree and timeline
criteria: Every step remains addressable
The same chosen step is identified coherently
Controls remain usable on supported layouts
cases.exception: Navigating a page must not select a different feature merely because a temporary row index changed.

cases.title: Edit a hole after its supporting body changes
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to edit a hole after its supporting body changes, so I can refine an earlier design and preserve its construction instead of rebuilding it from scratch.
steps: Create an attached Through all hole
Resize or rotate its source body
criteria: The hole follows the supporting face geometry
Its intended sketch dimensions remain
Through depth recalculates from the current body
cases.exception: If that face disappears or becomes ambiguous the app must retain the original and offer reselection or a fixed workplane choice.

cases.title: Pick real edges rather than triangle diagonals
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to pick real edges rather than triangle diagonals, so I can refine an earlier design and preserve its construction instead of rebuilding it from scratch.
steps: Choose an analytic cube cylinder and drilled solid
Tap straight edges circular rims and smooth seams
criteria: Geometric edges and whole circular rims are selectable
Triangle diagonals and smooth surface seams are excluded
Selected references remain identifiable
cases.exception: Picking a tessellated display edge is not acceptable if it changes unpredictably after a mesh rebuild.

cases.title: Toggle multiple edges and clear them
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to toggle multiple edges and clear them, so I can refine an earlier design and preserve its construction instead of rebuilding it from scratch.
steps: Use Select all edges and clear selection
criteria: The highlighted set matches the chosen references
Clear removes the set
Orbit drags do not add random edges
cases.exception: An empty edge selection must leave Preview finish unavailable or explain the prerequisite.

cases.title: Round a cube edge with a fillet
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to round a cube edge with a fillet, so I can refine an earlier design and preserve its construction instead of rebuilding it from scratch.
steps: Set a small known Fillet radius
Preview apply and inspect a section
criteria: The sharp corner is replaced by a real constant radius surface within tolerance
The result is closed
Apply is one Undo step
cases.exception: A smooth shaded sharp mesh is not an acceptable replacement for changed solid geometry.

cases.title: Bevel an edge with a chamfer
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to bevel an edge with a chamfer, so I can refine an earlier design and preserve its construction instead of rebuilding it from scratch.
steps: Select an edge and choose equal distance Chamfer
criteria: The two adjacent faces are cut back by the intended distance
The bevel is a real planar face
The remaining solid is closed
cases.exception: Chamfer distance must not be interpreted as the fillet radius or applied in display pixels.

cases.title: Finish circular rims and hole entrances
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to finish circular rims and hole entrances, so I can refine an earlier design and preserve its construction instead of rebuilding it from scratch.
steps: Pick an outer cylinder rim and a drilled hole entrance in separate copies
criteria: Whole concentric edge references are respected
The intended rim changes while unrelated rims do not
The bore remains as designed
cases.exception: Nested circular edges with similar radii must not silently swap because of mesh index ordering.

cases.title: Reselect the original edges of a finish
cases.story: As a confident maker, I want to reselect the original edges of a finish, so I can refine an earlier design and preserve its construction instead of rebuilding it from scratch.
steps: Edit an existing finish and choose Reselect edges
criteria: The picker shows the intact sharp source
The revised set belongs to that source
Cancel restores the saved finish and Apply rebuilds later features
